1	# Spec: the export hang in C5's fix pass — reproduce, find the cause, then fix (diagnosis)
2	
3	## Goal
4	Reproduce the `av1` MP4 hang (video pump in `copyNextSampleBuffer`, no compositor request seen) in a counted loop, in the probe and in a Release app over MCP. Name its cause from samples and request counters, then fix the app, or the harness alone, along the branch the evidence picks. STOP where this spec says to.
5	
6	## Files
7	Worktree `~/devel/framejob-codecs` (branch `codecs`). Never commit, push or merge.
8	Phase A, the instrument (always):
9	- `app/Sources/CompositorRequestCounts.swift` — NEW, all under `#if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`: process-wide request counters (Interfaces).
10	- `app/Sources/Compositor.swift` — wiring only, under `#if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`: `asked()` first in `startRequest`; `begun()` on entry to its `renderQueue` block, with `defer { done() }`; `cancelledAll()` in `cancelAllPendingVideoCompositionRequests`.
11	- `app/Sources/ExportProgressSheetController.swift` — a `#if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` read-only `devReading`.
12	- `app/Sources/AgentServer+ExportSheet.swift` — NEW dev tool `export_sheet`: handler and catalog row.
13	- `app/Sources/AgentServer+DevTools.swift` — register it in `devHandlers` and in `devTools()`'s rows, last. Not in `devOffMainTools`: it waits for nothing.
14	- `tools/proof/encoder_limit_probe.swift` — opt-in environment knobs (Interfaces). With none set, the answer is byte-for-byte what it is today.
15	- `tools/proof/export_hang_soak.py` — NEW loop runner and watchdog (Interfaces). Output goes to `tools/proof/work/export-hang/<YYYY-MM-DD>/`, which is gitignored by `tools/proof/.gitignore`'s `work/`.
16	- Docs for the new dev tool:
17	  - `tools/proof/dev_tools.py`: append `"export_sheet"` to `DEV_TOOLS` and add it to the docstring.
18	  - `designs/spec/07.9c-agent-graphics-dev-tools-transport.md`: one paragraph after `graphic_memory`'s. Update `designs/spec/README.md`'s Lines cells to match.
19	  - `app/CLAUDE.md`: a map entry for the two new files.
20	  - `docs/developing.md`: add it to the dev-tools list.
21	  - `tools/proof/README.md`: a section for the soak.
22	  - Root `CLAUDE.md`'s dev-tools sentence: the orchestrator applies this edit. Write the line you want in the notes.
23	Phase C, the fix. Touch only the files the chosen branch names (Approach step 6):
24	- branch R (re-entrancy): `app/Sources/ExportQueueController.swift`.
25	- branch P (pool or GCD starvation by app code): the file that holds the blocking work the samples name. Write its path in the notes before editing.
26	- branch B (a reader buffer held by the encode pump): `app/Sources/ExportEncodePump.swift` and/or `app/Sources/ExportI010.swift`.
27	- branch L (a lost compositor request): `app/Sources/Compositor.swift`.
28	- branch H (harness only): `tools/proof/encoder_limit_probe.swift`.
29	- Every branch: `tools/proof/encoder_limit_proof.py` (a new row and a mutant, the docstring, `PROBE_ROWS`, `MUTANTS`), `designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md` plus `11-decisions/README.md` (a §11 entry, only if a rule changes), `designs/codec-export.md` (the record), `tools/proof/README.md`, and issue #379 through `gh`.
30	- `app/Sources/Exporter.swift` is at 598 lines. If a branch needs it, a pure move out of it lands first and is gated alone (rule: ~600 cap).
31	
32	## Interfaces
33	```swift
34	#if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
35	enum CompositorRequestCounts {          // NSLock-guarded, every compositor instance in the process
36	    struct Snapshot: Equatable { let asked: Int; let begun: Int; let done: Int; let cancelAll: Int }
37	    static func asked(); static func begun(); static func done(); static func cancelledAll()
38	    static var snapshot: Snapshot { get }
39	}
40	// ExportProgressSheetController
41	var devReading: (finished: Bool, status: String, progress: Double) { get }   // didFinish, statusLabel, bar
42	// AgentServer
43	func exportSheet(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String
44	func exportSheetTool() -> [String: Any]
45	#endif
46	```
47	- `export_sheet` takes `action` (required: `"begin"`, `"status"` or `"close"`) and `project` (optional, resolved by `target(a)`).
48	  - `begin` also takes `preset` and `path` (required) and two optionals, `encoder_speed` and `physical_memory` (an integer of 0 or more).
49	    - It sets `ExportEncoderLedger.shared.physicalMemory` first when `physical_memory` is given; 0 restores `ProcessInfo`'s value.
50	    - It resolves the settings with `ReelExport.settings(project, preset:, overrides:)`, using the URL from `destinationURL` and `requireFolder`.
51	    - It refuses a window that already has a sheet.
52	    - It calls `editor.beginExport(settings:to:)`, which is exactly what Export…'s save panel calls.
53	    - It answers `{path, booked: [UInt64]}`.
54	  - `status` answers `{state: "none"|"running"|"finished", status, progress, ledger: [UInt64], compositor: {asked, begun, done, cancel_all}}`.
55	  - `close` dismisses a finished sheet and refuses a running one. It answers `{closed: true}`.
56	- Probe knobs, read from the environment:
57	  - `RC_PROBE_TRACE=<path>`: a main-run-loop `Timer` (1 s) plus every `Watch.tick` append one JSON line: `{t, row, seq, sheet:{finished, progress}, jobs:[{id, state, progress}], ledger, compositor}`.
58	  - `RC_PROBE_HOLD_POOL=<n>`: for Q1's whole length, n `Task.detached` bodies each block on a semaphore. They are released after Q1.
59	  - `RC_PROBE_A_PRESET=<id>`: A's preset (default `av1`), used as a control.
60	- `python3 tools/proof/export_hang_soak.py --mode probe|app --runs N [--load K] [--stall-s S] [--variant NAME] [--app debug|release]`
61	  - `--load K` starts K `/usr/bin/yes > /dev/null` children and kills them at exit, in a `finally` block and on a signal.
62	  - `--stall-s` (default 120) is how long no job's state or progress, and not the sheet's progress, may change before a run counts as a stall.
63	  - On a stall, the runner:
64	    - takes `sample <pid> 10 -file sample-<run>.txt`, waits 30 s, and samples again;
65	    - records the trace's last compositor counts;
66	    - kills only its own pid.
67	  - It writes `summary.json` with, per run: the variant, the load average at start and end, the outcome (`done`, `stall` or `error`), the seconds taken, and the stall's classification. The classification is token counts over the second sample (`copyNextSampleBuffer`, `Compositor`, `FigSemaphoreWait`, `cooperative`, `usleep`, `waitUntilCompleted`, `svt_`, `semaphore_wait`), plus the main thread's top five frames and the total thread count.
68	  - `probe` mode builds through `encoder_limit_proof.build_probe` and reuses it. A `--variant` is a source copy with an anchor replaced, built the way `encoder_limit_proof`'s mutants are, with each anchor found exactly once.
69	  - `app` mode works as follows:
70	    - It starts one owned instance (`mcp.launch` via `proof_app.executable`) per 10 runs and relaunches after a stall.
71	    - It makes A1 (`av1_export_proof.av_doc`) and W9 (`webm_export_proof.long_doc`) once per instance.
72	    - Each run then does these steps:
73	      1. `export_sheet begin` W9 `av1` `smaller`, with `physical_memory` = 4 × that job's cost, taken from the probe's P0 tables through `encoder_limit_proof.Tables`;
74	      2. `export` A (`av1`), B and C (`h264`) of A1;
75	      3. wait until everything finishes, polling `export_sheet status` and `export_status` once a second;
76	      4. `export` two `av1` jobs of A1 back to back, which is Q5's re-entrant launch;
77	      5. `export_sheet close`, then `physical_memory` 0.
78	
79	## Approach
80	1. Build the Phase A instrument. Run `make typecheck`, the probe typecheck and `make app` (Release). Smoke-test with `--mode probe --runs 1 --load 0` and `--mode app --runs 1 --load 0`.
81	2. **Baseline.** All soaks run in the background with one bounded wait, never a poll loop.
82	   - The probe: 30 runs at `--load 24` and 10 at `--load 0`.
83	   - The app: 15 runs at `--load 24` and 5 at `--load 0`.
84	   - If there are fewer than 3 stalls in total, add 30 probe runs at `--load 36`.
85	   - **STOP-1:** zero stalls across all runs. Write the counts and the instrument into the record, leave #379 open with the counts, and stop for a ruling.
86	3. **Classify** each stall with the counters and the second sample. "AVF" means AVFoundation.
87	
88	   | Branch | Counters | Sample |
89	   |---|---|---|
90	   | P | `asked > begun` (asked, never run) | the GCD/cooperative workers exhausted, many threads parked (#367's signature) |
91	   | L | `begun > done` and no Compositor frame (lost request) | — |

93	   | A | `asked == done` (AVF never asked) | AVF/VT threads in `FigSemaphoreWait`; then R, B or AVF itself, settled by step 4 |
94	4. **Variants.** Run each variant at the baseline's load until it has run as many runs as the baseline needed for 3 stalls, and never fewer than 30. "Removes" means 0 stalls in those runs.
95	   - `defer-launch`: in `ExportQueueController`, `ledgerChanged` runs `start()` one main turn later. This tests R.
96	   - `slot-before-read`: `ExportEncodePump` waits for a slot before `copyNextSampleBuffer`. This tests B.
97	   - `flush-after`: `ExportI010Converter` flushes its texture cache right after `waitUntilCompleted`. This tests B.
98	   - `RC_PROBE_HOLD_POOL=12`: does the stall rate jump? This tests P.
99	   - `RC_PROBE_A_PRESET=h264`: does the stall need the encode pump at all?
100	5. **STOP-2:** the stall is inside AVFoundation and no variant removes it, or the only cure is a watchdog that fails a stuck export. A stuck export is a read that never returns, which G-17 accepts; a watchdog would re-litigate G-17 and CX-18 (6). Record the evidence and stop for a ruling.
101	   **STOP-3:** the fix would change the queue's one-at-a-time rule or let a sheet be held (CX-18 (6)).
102	6. **Fix along the branch.**
103	   - R: a held job launches on the main turn after the booking that freed it ends, never inside `end`. This amends CX-18, so write a §11 entry before the code.
104	   - P: the app's blocking work moves off the pool or is bounded (#367's rule). Add a §11 entry if a rule is new.
105	   - B: no reader buffer is held across a wait.
106	   - L: every path answers its request.
107	   - H: fix the harness. The record says exactly why the app cannot reach the probe's state, citing the app loop's counts.
108	7. **Proof row.** Add one deterministic probe row (Q6) that fails on the old behaviour. For R: A is still `.waiting` when the sheet's `end` returns and `.running` one main turn later. Add one mutant that restores the old line; it must be CAUGHT on Q6 alone. If a branch admits no deterministic row, say why in the notes; the mutant is then scored by the soak, run at the baseline's counts.
109	8. **After.** Re-run step 2's baseline counts on the fixed tree; the target is 0 stalls. Settle #379:
110	   - same signature (encode pump, same branch): close it with the before and after counts;
111	   - otherwise comment what was learnt and leave it open.
112	   Write `designs/codec-export.md` "## Export hang (C5's fix pass)", placed after C6a's section, with the baseline and after counts per mode, load and variant, the samples' classification, the branch, and what is owed.
113	9. Kill every `yes` child and every instance you started, by pid, so the machine is left idle for C6b.
114	
115	## Constraints
116	- G-17 and #378 (`designs/spec/11-decisions/graphics.md`, `deepening.md`): a reader is cancelled only by its own pump, on its own queue, after its last read. Never call `cancelReading` from another thread.
117	- #367: no synchronous `AVAssetReader` read on the Swift cooperative pool. Only `MediaImporter.swift` and `SpeechEngine.swift` use `Task`.
118	- CX-18 (`ExportQueueController.start/launch/finished`, `ExportProgressSheetController.viewDidAppear/finished`, `ExportEncoderLedger`), on the main thread only:
119	  - `begin` books before `exporter.export`;
120	  - `finished` clears its token before `end`;
121	  - `isLaunching` guards against re-entrancy.
122	  - Keep the `begin-late` and `token-overwrite` mutants caught.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Object types: Mesh, Curve, Su… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

While auto mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. The choice is yours: prefer Edit or Write when a shell edit would be fragile, such as exact or multi-line replacements, or sed/awk flags that differ between GNU and BSD/macOS.

7	/// One `AVVideoComposition` instruction, carrying the `RecipeSource` slot the
8	/// frames inside it must be read from (spec §7.5).
9	///
10	/// The key is why this type exists instead of `AVVideoCompositionInstruction`:
11	/// `AVFoundation` instantiates ONE compositor object per player item and hands
12	/// it nothing about the document, so with a process-wide "current project" two
13	/// open windows would render each other's frames. The key travels on the
14	/// instruction, which the request hands back, so a document can only ever read
15	/// its own recipe. `mediaURLs` rides along for the same reason — an `image`
16	/// layer names a media id and only the document knows the file.
17	final class RecipeInstruction: NSObject, AVVideoCompositionInstructionProtocol {
18	    let timeRange: CMTimeRange
19	    let enablePostProcessing: Bool = false
20	    /// True: a transition changes every frame inside its instruction, so
21	    /// AVFoundation must not reuse one composed frame across the range.
22	    let containsTweening: Bool = true
23	    // `nonisolated(unsafe)`: the protocol is `Sendable` and `NSValue` is not,
24	    // but this array is built once in `init` and never mutated, which is the
25	    // exact case the attribute exists for.
26	    nonisolated(unsafe) let requiredSourceTrackIDs: [NSValue]?
27	    /// Never a passthrough: every frame goes through the Metal pipeline, even
28	    /// a single full-frame layer, so opacity and colour edits show without a
29	    /// composition rebuild (§7.6).
30	    let passthroughTrackID: CMPersistentTrackID = kCMPersistentTrackID_Invalid
31	
32	    /// The document's `RecipeSource` slot (`RecipeSource.swift`) — or an
33	    /// export's own, which is a fresh one. It names the project a frame is
34	    /// composed from AND, since phase 7, the `RecipeOptions` that project is
35	    /// asked with, so an option never has to be threaded through the
36	    /// instruction.
37	    let recipeKey: Int
38	    /// Media id → file, for `image` layers. Same map `CompositionBuilder`
39	    /// resolved the composition's assets from.
40	    let mediaURLs: [UInt32: URL]
41	    /// Composition video track id → the source orientation code
42	    /// (`CompositionBuilder.orientationCode`) of whatever that track is
43	    /// showing across THIS instruction. Per instruction because an
44	    /// instruction boundary falls wherever the visible clips change (§7.2),
45	    /// so within one, a track shows exactly one clip.
46	    let sourceOrientations: [Int: Int]
47	    /// Clips whose media file is gone (spec §5.6). A `track` layer with no
48	    /// source frame is normally just a gap, so the compositor cannot tell the
49	    /// two apart on its own — the plan can, because it knows which media each
50	    /// clip's segment came from and `urls` says which of those resolved.
51	    /// These get the slate instead of nothing.
52	    let missingClips: Set<UInt32>
53	    /// Composition video track ids whose segment across THIS instruction is a
54	    /// full-range media (spec §11 GR-22): a log curve's code domain follows
55	    /// it. Per instruction for `sourceOrientations`' reason; empty when no
56	    /// segment converts with a log curve.
57	    let fullRangeTracks: Set<Int>
58	
59	    init(
60	        timeRange: CMTimeRange, requiredTrackIDs: [Int], recipeKey: Int,
61	        mediaURLs: [UInt32: URL], sourceOrientations: [Int: Int],
62	        missingClips: Set<UInt32>, fullRangeTracks: Set<Int> = []
63	    ) {
64	        self.timeRange = timeRange
65	        self.requiredSourceTrackIDs = requiredTrackIDs.map {
66	            NSNumber(value: CMPersistentTrackID($0))
67	        }
68	        self.recipeKey = recipeKey
69	        self.mediaURLs = mediaURLs
70	        self.sourceOrientations = sourceOrientations
71	        self.missingClips = missingClips
72	        self.fullRangeTracks = fullRangeTracks
73	        super.init()
74	    }

76	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
77	        fatalError("RecipeInstruction does not support NSCoder")
78	    }

81	/// Why a frame could not be composed. Every one is reported through
82	/// `request.finish(with:)` — AVFoundation then drops that frame and keeps
83	/// playing, which is the whole point: a compositor that throws or traps takes
84	/// the player down with it.
85	enum CompositorError: LocalizedError {
86	    case metalUnavailable
87	    case noPixelBuffer
88	    case noDestinationTexture

91	        switch self {
92	        case .metalUnavailable: return "Metal is not available on this system."
93	        case .noPixelBuffer: return "The render context ran out of pixel buffers."
94	        case .noDestinationTexture: return "The frame buffer could not be used as a texture."

100	/// back to front, source-over into the destination.
101	///
102	/// AVFoundation creates this object itself (`customVideoCompositorClass`), so
103	/// it can take no arguments — everything per-document arrives on the
104	/// instruction. Requests are served on one serial queue and every exit path

180	    func renderContextChanged(_ newRenderContext: AVVideoCompositionRenderContext) {
181	        lock.lock()
182	        renderContext = newRenderContext
183	        lock.unlock()
184	        renderer?.flushPixelBufferTextures()
185	    }
186	
187	    func startRequest(_ asyncVideoCompositionRequest: AVAsynchronousVideoCompositionRequest) {
188	        renderQueue.async { [weak self] in
189	            guard let self = self else {
190	                asyncVideoCompositionRequest.finishCancelledRequest()
191	                return
192	            }
193	            guard !self.isCancelled else {
194	                asyncVideoCompositionRequest.finishCancelledRequest()
195	                return
196	            }
197	            self.serve(asyncVideoCompositionRequest)
198	        }
199	    }
200	
201	    /// Flushes the queue: the cancelled flag makes every request already
202	    /// queued answer `finishCancelledRequest`, and the empty `sync` waits for
203	    /// the one in flight. AVFoundation calls this on a seek and at teardown,
204	    /// and requires that no request be left unanswered.
205	    func cancelAllPendingVideoCompositionRequests() {
206	        setCancelled(true)
207	        renderQueue.sync {}
208	        setCancelled(false)
209	    }
210	
211	    // MARK: - Serving one frame
212	
213	    private func serve(_ request: AVAsynchronousVideoCompositionRequest) {
214	        let started = CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent()
215	        guard let renderer = renderer else {
216	            request.finish(with: CompositorError.metalUnavailable)
217	            return
218	        }
219	        guard let destination = request.renderContext.newPixelBuffer() else {
220	            request.finish(with: CompositorError.noPixelBuffer)
221	            return
222	        }
223	        let instruction = request.videoCompositionInstruction as? RecipeInstruction
224	        let key = instruction?.recipeKey ?? 0
225	        let ticks = CompositionBuilder.ticks(request.compositionTime)
226	        // A playing preview's prefetch follows the frame asked for (G-36 (d)).
227	        GraphicPrefetch.shared.reach(key, ticks: ticks)
228	        // The key is the whole ask: `RecipeSource.recipe(for:at:)` reads the
229	        // project AND that key's `RecipeOptions` under one hold, so a burn-in
230	        // an export asked for arrives here without this file, the
231	        // instruction or `CompositionBuilder` carrying a flag of its own
232	        // (spec §7.3). Do not read the two halves separately.
233	        let recipe = RecipeSource.shared.recipe(for: key, at: ticks)
234	        do {
235	            try renderer.render(
236	                recipe: recipe, into: destination, request: request, instruction: instruction,
237	                converts: canConformColorOfSourceFrames)
238	            request.finish(withComposedVideoFrame: destination)
239	            #if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
240	            PlaybackTrials.shared.served(
241	                key, ticks: ticks, seconds: CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent() - started,
242	                buffer: destination)
243	            #endif
244	            WaveformTaps.shared.offer(
245	                destination, key: instruction?.recipeKey ?? 0,
246	                signal: ScopeSignal(canvas: recipe?.canvas))
247	        } catch {
248	            // A frame that will not compose is dropped: the player shows the last one.
249	            request.finish(with: error)
250	        }
251	        record(CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent() - started)
252	    }
253	
254	    // MARK: - Timing log
255	
256	    /// Averages over a two-second window (120 frames) and reports the worst
257	    /// frame in it, which is the number that matters — an 8 ms budget with a
258	    /// 40 ms outlier every second still stutters (§7.5).
259	    private func record(_ seconds: Double) {
260	        guard Compositor.timingEnabled else { return }
261	        lock.lock()
262	        frames += 1
263	        totalSeconds += seconds
264	        worstSeconds = max(worstSeconds, seconds)
265	        let due = frames >= 120
266	        let average = totalSeconds / Double(max(frames, 1)) * 1000
267	        let worst = worstSeconds * 1000
268	        if due {
269	            frames = 0
270	            totalSeconds = 0
271	            worstSeconds = 0
272	        }
273	        lock.unlock()
274	        if due {
275	            // Step 0's passes over the same window (spec §11 GR-15): 0 for a
276	            // frame with no converted source. Appended, so the line's prefix
277	            // stays what the proofs' timing pattern reads.
278	            let passes = renderer?.inputs.takePassCount() ?? 0
279	            NSLog("[framejob] compositor: %.2f ms average, %.2f ms worst over 120 frames, "
280	                + "%ld input passes", average, worst, passes)
281	        }
282	    }
283	
284	    private var isCancelled: Bool {
285	        lock.lock()
286	        defer { lock.unlock() }
287	        return cancelled
288	    }
289	
290	    private func setCancelled(_ value: Bool) {
291	        lock.lock()
292	        cancelled = value
293	        lock.unlock()
294	    }
295	}

3	/// The sheet that stays up for the write itself: a bar, a Cancel that really
4	/// stops the session, and — once the file lands — the result and a Show in
5	/// Finder (spec §10 step 10).
6	///
7	/// It owns the `Exporter`, which is why the export survives everything the
8	/// editor does next: the sheet is retained by the presenting controller for
9	/// as long as it is on screen, and nothing else holds the session.
10	///
11	/// Its own file rather than the foot of `ExportSheetController.swift`, which
12	/// stood at 1114 lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap. The seam is where
13	/// the two sheets stop having anything in common: the settings card is a
14	/// conversation with the core — every number it shows comes back from
15	/// `rc_export_settings`, and its controls only decide what to ask for — and
16	/// this one has already finished asking. It holds a project handle, a URL and
17	/// an `Exporter`, watches one number climb, and turns into its own result
18	/// panel; nothing on it can change what is being written.
19	///
20	/// Being a separate CLASS is what makes the cut free. `private` on an
21	/// extension member reaches only its own file, so splitting a type across
22	/// files costs every crossing member its privacy — the price
23	/// `ExporterLoudness.swift` records paying, and the price the two `extension
24	/// ExportSheetController` files beside this one pay. A type carries its own
25	/// scope, so every member below keeps the visibility it had, and
26	/// `EditorViewController+Export.swift` presenting it is the only name that
27	/// crosses.
28	final class ExportProgressSheetController: NSViewController {
29	    private let exporter = Exporter()
30	    /// The project handle as the export was confirmed. Handles are immutable
31	    /// (spec §5.5), so edits made after this point cannot reach the file.
32	    private let project: ReelProject
33	    private let urls: [UInt32: URL]
34	    private let settings: ExportSettings
35	    private let destination: URL
36	    /// What the export asks of the RECIPE rather than of the settings — the
37	    /// timecode burn-in (spec §7.3, road map 2's phase 7). It is a separate
38	    /// argument because it is a separate question: `ExportSettings` is what
39	    /// `rc_export_settings` resolved, and an option posted through the
40	    /// override table would be dropped in silence and the file reported a
41	    /// success. Defaulted, so a caller that does not burn in is written the
42	    /// way it always was.
43	    private let options: RecipeOptions
44	    /// The document's compiled graphics as the export was confirmed (G-13),
45	    /// pinned by `Exporter.export` for the write.
46	    private let graphics: GraphicSet?
47	
48	    private let bar = NSProgressIndicator()
49	    private let statusLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "Preparing…")
50	    private let percentLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: "0 %")
51	    /// Set in `loadView`; the only implicitly-unwrapped optionals the file has
52	    /// (app/CLAUDE.md allows them for exactly this).
53	    private var stopButton: NSButton!
54	    private var revealButton: NSButton!
55	
56	    private var didStart = false
57	    private var didFinish = false
58	    /// This export's booking in the encoder ledger (spec §11 CX-18): counted, never held —
59	    /// a person who chose Export… asked to write now. nil on an AVFoundation row and once
60	    /// it is over.
61	    private var ledgerToken: UInt64?
62	
63	    init(
64	        project: ReelProject, urls: [UInt32: URL], settings: ExportSettings, to url: URL,
65	        options: RecipeOptions = .none, graphics: GraphicSet? = nil
66	    ) {
67	        self.project = project
68	        self.urls = urls
69	        self.settings = settings
70	        self.destination = url
71	        self.options = options
72	        self.graphics = graphics
73	        super.init(nibName: nil, bundle: nil)
74	    }
75	
76	    @available(*, unavailable)
77	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
78	        fatalError("ExportProgressSheetController does not support NSCoder")
79	    }
80	
81	    deinit {
82	        let token = ledgerToken
83	        ledgerToken = nil
84	        ExportEncoderLedger.shared.end(token)
85	    }
86	
87	    override func loadView() {
88	        styleSheetProgressBar(bar)
89	
90	        styleSheetStatusLabel(statusLabel)
91	        statusLabel.stringValue = "Preparing “\(destination.lastPathComponent)”…"
92	
93	        percentLabel.font = DS.mono(11)
94	        percentLabel.textColor = DS.textFaint
95	
96	        let content = makeProgressStack([bar, statusLabel, percentLabel])
97	
98	        stopButton = StickerButton(
99	            title: "Cancel", style: .secondary, target: self, action: #selector(stopClicked(_:)))
100	        revealButton = StickerButton(
101	            title: "Show in Finder", style: .primary, target: self,
102	            action: #selector(revealClicked(_:)))
103	        hideReturnTarget(revealButton)
104	
105	        view = makeSheetView(
106	            title: "Exporting",
107	            content: content,
108	            buttonRow: makeButtonRow(cancel: stopButton, apply: revealButton))
109	    }
110	
111	    override func viewDidAppear() {
112	        super.viewDidAppear()
113	        guard !didStart else { return }
114	        didStart = true
115	        // Booked BEFORE `export`, whose early refusals finish synchronously inside it.
116	        ledgerToken = ExportEncoderLedger.shared.begin(settings)
117	        exporter.export(
118	            project: project, urls: urls, settings: settings, to: destination, options: options,
119	            graphics: graphics,
120	            progress: { [weak self] value in self?.progressed(value) },
121	            completion: { [weak self] result in self?.finished(result) })
122	    }
123	
124	    // MARK: - Exporter callbacks
125	
126	    private func progressed(_ value: Double) {
127	        guard !didFinish else { return }
128	        let clamped = min(max(value, 0), 1)
129	        bar.doubleValue = clamped
130	        percentLabel.stringValue = "\(Int((clamped * 100).rounded())) %"
131	        // The exporter names its own phase while it has one. Without this the
132	        // label would claim to be writing a file during the loudness
133	        // measurement — which on an audio-only export is half the wait, and
134	        // the half where nothing is on disk yet.
135	        if let phase = exporter.phaseDescription {
136	            statusLabel.stringValue = phase
137	        } else if clamped > 0 {
138	            statusLabel.stringValue = "Writing “\(destination.lastPathComponent)”…"
139	        }
140	    }
141	
142	    /// The one exit for all three outcomes. Cancelling closes the sheet and
143	    /// removes the half-written file; success and failure both turn the sheet
144	    /// into its own result panel rather than trading it for an alert.
145	    private func finished(_ result: Result<URL, any Error>) {
146	        didFinish = true
147	        // Cleared before `end`, whose post may launch a held queue job.
148	        let token = ledgerToken
149	        ledgerToken = nil
150	        ExportEncoderLedger.shared.end(token)
151	        stopButton.isEnabled = true
152	        switch result {
153	        case .success(let url):
154	            bar.doubleValue = 1
155	            percentLabel.stringValue = "100 %"
156	            // What the file actually holds, normalised or not: the export
157	            // measured its own mix on the way through, so the numbers are a
158	            // report rather than a promise.
159	            let measured = exporter.loudnessReport.map { " \($0.summary)." } ?? ""
160	            // What the graphics warned while the file was drawn: a count on
161	            // the line, the list in its tooltip (G-24 (c)).
162	            let warnings = exporter.graphicWarnings
163	            statusLabel.stringValue = "Exported “\(url.lastPathComponent)”.\(measured)"
164	                + Exporter.graphicWarningSuffix(warnings)
165	            statusLabel.toolTip = Exporter.graphicWarningDetails(warnings)
166	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
167	            stopButton.title = "Close"
168	            revealButton.isHidden = false
169	            revealButton.isEnabled = true
170	        case .failure(let error):
171	            if case Exporter.ExportError.cancelled = error {
172	                try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination)
173	                dismiss(self)
174	                return
175	            }
176	            bar.doubleValue = 0
177	            percentLabel.stringValue = ""
178	            statusLabel.stringValue = error.localizedDescription
179	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
180	            stopButton.title = "Close"
181	        }
182	    }
183	
184	    // MARK: - Buttons
185	
186	    /// Cancel while it runs, Close once it is over. One button because there
187	    /// is only ever one thing to do with a sheet that is busy.
188	    @objc private func stopClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
189	        guard !didFinish else {
190	            dismiss(self)
191	            return
192	        }
193	        stopButton.isEnabled = false
194	        statusLabel.stringValue = "Stopping…"
195	        exporter.cancel()
196	    }
197	
198	    @objc private func revealClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
199	        guard didFinish else { return }
200	        NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([destination])
201	        dismiss(self)
202	    }
203	}

3	// MARK: - The dev-tools seam: tools compiled only under FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
4	
5	/// Where the dev tools live (road map 11, spec §11 V-1 and V-2).
6	///
7	/// **The flag.** `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` is a Swift compilation condition that
8	/// Debug and Release set and the Distribution configuration does not
9	/// (`project.yml`), so every proof and agent session, which launch Release,
10	/// has the dev tools and the binary `make dist` builds has none of their
11	/// code (V-1). A dev tool is an ORDINARY tool (V-2): a handler in
12	/// `devHandlers`, a row from `devTools()`, and nothing else — the parity
13	/// check, the argument gate and the schema checks cover it as they cover a
14	/// product tool, in both builds, because both tables are merged before any
15	/// of them reads.
16	///
17	/// **Why the check greps a marker, not tool names.** Swift string literals
18	/// of 15 UTF-8 bytes or fewer are stored inline in the code of an `-O`
19	/// binary, not as contiguous bytes, so a short tool name such as
20	/// `snapshot_ui` (11) can never be found in either build and an absence
21	/// check on it would pass for nothing. `tools/proof/dist_check.py` reads
22	/// `devToolsMarker` out of this file instead — at least 16 bytes — and
23	/// requires it present in Release's binary and absent from Distribution's.
24	///
25	/// **What keeps the marker live.** The flag-on `devTools()` logs it, so the
26	/// optimiser cannot drop the literal. V2 adds rows and handlers here with no
27	/// edit to the check.
28	///
29	/// **Where the rows go.** `catalogJSON()` splices `devTools()` in
30	/// immediately BEFORE the file tools, never at the end: the catalog's last
31	/// eleven names are the file group plus `record_screen`, which
32	/// `recording_probe.py` asserts. Swift takes no `#if` inside a dictionary
33	/// literal, so `AgentServer.swift` merges `devHandlers` through
34	/// `withDevHandlers` and `devOffMainTools` by a union, one line each.
35	extension AgentServer {
36	    typealias ToolHandler = (AgentServer) -> ([String: Any]) throws -> String
37	
38	    /// `product` with `devHandlers` merged in. A dev tool that reuses a
39	    /// product tool's name keeps the PRODUCT handler and complains the way
40	    /// the startup parity check does.
41	    static func withDevHandlers(_ product: [String: ToolHandler]) -> [String: ToolHandler] {
42	        var merged = product
43	        for (name, handler) in devHandlers.sorted(by: { $0.key < $1.key }) {
44	            if merged[name] != nil {
45	                let msg = "dev tool \(name) reuses a product tool's name"
46	                assertionFailure(msg)
47	                NSLog("Frame Job: %@", msg)
48	                continue
49	            }
50	            merged[name] = handler
51	        }
52	        return merged
53	    }
54	
55	    /// Every dev tool's name, in either build (empty in Distribution): the
56	    /// assistant withholds each one (spec §11 AI-7, `AssistantToolTable`).
57	    static var devToolNames: Set<String> { Set(devHandlers.keys) }
58	
59	    #if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
60	    // dist_check.py parses the next line (D1) and requires it bare — nothing after the
61	    // closing quote — at least 16 bytes, present in Release's binary, absent from Distribution's.
62	    static let devToolsMarker = "framejob-dev-tools-compiled-in"
63	
64	    private static let devHandlers: [String: ToolHandler] = [
65	        // AgentServer+Snapshot.swift
66	        "snapshot_ui": { $0.snapshotUI },
67	        // AgentServer+MenuItem.swift
68	        "perform_menu_item": { $0.performMenuItem },
69	        "cancel_sheet": { $0.cancelSheet },
70	        // AgentServer+InspectorTab.swift
71	        "select_inspector_tab": { $0.selectInspectorTab },
72	        // AgentServer+Assistant.swift
73	        "assistant_send": { $0.assistantSend },
74	        "assistant_answer": { $0.assistantAnswer },
75	        // AgentServer+PlayPreview.swift
76	        "play_preview": { $0.playPreview },
77	        // AgentServer+GraphicMemory.swift
78	        "graphic_memory": { $0.graphicMemory },
79	    ]
80	
81	    static let devOffMainTools: Set<String> = [
82	        "snapshot_ui", "perform_menu_item", "cancel_sheet", "assistant_send", "assistant_answer",
83	        "play_preview", "graphic_memory",
84	    ]
85	
86	    /// The dev tools' catalog rows, in catalog order: `snapshot_ui` (V2a),
87	    /// `perform_menu_item` and `cancel_sheet` (V2b), `select_inspector_tab`
88	    /// (V3), `assistant_send` and `assistant_answer` (road map 12 A1),
89	    /// `play_preview` (issue #127, G-36), `graphic_memory` (issue #127,
90	    /// G-37). The log is what keeps `devToolsMarker` in the optimised binary;
91	    /// it never says `Frame Job: `, the prefix a proof reads as the parity
92	    /// check complaining.
93	    func devTools() -> [[String: Any]] {
94	        let rows: [[String: Any]] = [
95	            snapshotUITool(), performMenuItemTool(), cancelSheetTool(), selectInspectorTabTool(),
96	            assistantSendTool(), assistantAnswerTool(), playPreviewTool(), graphicMemoryTool(),
97	        ]
98	        NSLog("Frame Job agent server: %@, %ld dev tools", Self.devToolsMarker, rows.count)
99	        return rows
100	    }
101	    #else
102	    private static let devHandlers: [String: ToolHandler] = [:]
103	
104	    static let devOffMainTools: Set<String> = []
105	
106	    /// Distribution ships no dev tools.
107	    func devTools() -> [[String: Any]] {
108	        []
109	    }
110	    #endif
111	}

7	/// One `AVVideoComposition` instruction, carrying the `RecipeSource` slot the
8	/// frames inside it must be read from (spec §7.5).
9	///
10	/// The key is why this type exists instead of `AVVideoCompositionInstruction`:
11	/// `AVFoundation` instantiates ONE compositor object per player item and hands
12	/// it nothing about the document, so with a process-wide "current project" two
13	/// open windows would render each other's frames. The key travels on the
14	/// instruction, which the request hands back, so a document can only ever read
15	/// its own recipe. `mediaURLs` rides along for the same reason — an `image`
16	/// layer names a media id and only the document knows the file.
17	final class RecipeInstruction: NSObject, AVVideoCompositionInstructionProtocol {
18	    let timeRange: CMTimeRange
19	    let enablePostProcessing: Bool = false
20	    /// True: a transition changes every frame inside its instruction, so
21	    /// AVFoundation must not reuse one composed frame across the range.
22	    let containsTweening: Bool = true
23	    // `nonisolated(unsafe)`: the protocol is `Sendable` and `NSValue` is not,
24	    // but this array is built once in `init` and never mutated, which is the
25	    // exact case the attribute exists for.
26	    nonisolated(unsafe) let requiredSourceTrackIDs: [NSValue]?
27	    /// Never a passthrough: every frame goes through the Metal pipeline, even
28	    /// a single full-frame layer, so opacity and colour edits show without a
29	    /// composition rebuild (§7.6).
30	    let passthroughTrackID: CMPersistentTrackID = kCMPersistentTrackID_Invalid
31	
32	    /// The document's `RecipeSource` slot (`RecipeSource.swift`) — or an
33	    /// export's own, which is a fresh one. It names the project a frame is
34	    /// composed from AND, since phase 7, the `RecipeOptions` that project is
35	    /// asked with, so an option never has to be threaded through the
36	    /// instruction.
37	    let recipeKey: Int
38	    /// Media id → file, for `image` layers. Same map `CompositionBuilder`
39	    /// resolved the composition's assets from.
40	    let mediaURLs: [UInt32: URL]
41	    /// Composition video track id → the source orientation code
42	    /// (`CompositionBuilder.orientationCode`) of whatever that track is
43	    /// showing across THIS instruction. Per instruction because an
44	    /// instruction boundary falls wherever the visible clips change (§7.2),
45	    /// so within one, a track shows exactly one clip.
46	    let sourceOrientations: [Int: Int]
47	    /// Clips whose media file is gone (spec §5.6). A `track` layer with no
48	    /// source frame is normally just a gap, so the compositor cannot tell the
49	    /// two apart on its own — the plan can, because it knows which media each
50	    /// clip's segment came from and `urls` says which of those resolved.
51	    /// These get the slate instead of nothing.
52	    let missingClips: Set<UInt32>
53	    /// Composition video track ids whose segment across THIS instruction is a
54	    /// full-range media (spec §11 GR-22): a log curve's code domain follows
55	    /// it. Per instruction for `sourceOrientations`' reason; empty when no
56	    /// segment converts with a log curve.
57	    let fullRangeTracks: Set<Int>
58	
59	    init(
60	        timeRange: CMTimeRange, requiredTrackIDs: [Int], recipeKey: Int,
61	        mediaURLs: [UInt32: URL], sourceOrientations: [Int: Int],
62	        missingClips: Set<UInt32>, fullRangeTracks: Set<Int> = []
63	    ) {
64	        self.timeRange = timeRange
65	        self.requiredSourceTrackIDs = requiredTrackIDs.map {
66	            NSNumber(value: CMPersistentTrackID($0))
67	        }
68	        self.recipeKey = recipeKey
69	        self.mediaURLs = mediaURLs
70	        self.sourceOrientations = sourceOrientations
71	        self.missingClips = missingClips
72	        self.fullRangeTracks = fullRangeTracks
73	        super.init()
74	    }
75	
76	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
77	        fatalError("RecipeInstruction does not support NSCoder")
78	    }
79	}
80	
81	/// Why a frame could not be composed. Every one is reported through
82	/// `request.finish(with:)` — AVFoundation then drops that frame and keeps
83	/// playing, which is the whole point: a compositor that throws or traps takes
84	/// the player down with it.
85	enum CompositorError: LocalizedError {
86	    case metalUnavailable
87	    case noPixelBuffer
88	    case noDestinationTexture
89	
90	    var errorDescription: String? {
91	        switch self {
92	        case .metalUnavailable: return "Metal is not available on this system."
93	        case .noPixelBuffer: return "The render context ran out of pixel buffers."
94	        case .noDestinationTexture: return "The frame buffer could not be used as a texture."
95	        }
96	    }
97	}
98	
99	/// The custom compositor (spec §7.5): one Metal pipeline, one pass per layer,
100	/// back to front, source-over into the destination.
101	///
102	/// AVFoundation creates this object itself (`customVideoCompositorClass`), so
103	/// it can take no arguments — everything per-document arrives on the
104	/// instruction. Requests are served on one serial queue and every exit path
105	/// answers the request exactly once.
106	class Compositor: NSObject, AVVideoCompositing {
107	
108	    /// `defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob FrameJobCompositorTiming -bool YES`
109	    /// turns on the per-frame timing log — the measurement M1 step 5 is
110	    /// verified with ("playback stays at 60 fps on a 1080p source").
111	    static let timingDefaultsKey = "FrameJobCompositorTiming"
112	
113	    private static let timingEnabled = UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey: timingDefaultsKey)
114	
115	    /// The one documented GCD seam on this side (app/CLAUDE.md): AVFoundation
116	    /// calls `startRequest` from its own threads and expects the work to be
117	    /// asynchronous, and a serial queue is what keeps GPU submission ordered.
118	    private let renderQueue = DispatchQueue(
119	        label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.compositor", qos: .userInitiated)
120	
121	    private let renderer: MetalRenderer?
122	    private let lock = NSLock()
123	    private var renderContext: AVVideoCompositionRenderContext?
124	    private var cancelled = false
125	    private var frames = 0
126	    private var totalSeconds = 0.0
127	    private var worstSeconds = 0.0
128	
129	    override init() {
130	        renderer = MetalRenderer()
131	        super.init()
132	    }
133	
134	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
135	        fatalError("Compositor does not support NSCoder")
136	    }
137	
138	    // MARK: - AVVideoCompositing
139	
140	    /// The render context's buffers: 16-bit float, so a blend or a deep
141	    /// source keeps more than 256 levels a channel (spec §11 PR-1). The
142	    /// working format of every target a layer pipeline draws into follows it
143	    /// (`MetalRenderer.workingFormat`), and the export reader reads it.
144	    static let outputPixelFormat: OSType = REDACTED
145	    /// What every video source is decoded to: 16-bit float, so a 10-bit source
146	    /// keeps its levels; the layer stage clamps its values (spec §11 PR-2).
147	    static let sourcePixelFormat: OSType = REDACTED
148	
149	    /// Metal-compatible `sourcePixelFormat`, sampled through `texture(from:)`.
150	    /// AVFoundation converts any other pixel format; for a
151	    /// `ConvertingCompositor` not colour: an HDR or wide-gamut frame arrives
152	    /// native and labelled, and step 0 converts it (spec §11 GR-15, §7.5).
153	    var sourcePixelBufferAttributes: [String: any Sendable]? {
154	        [
155	            kCVPixelBufferPixelFormatTypeKey as String: Int(Compositor.sourcePixelFormat),
156	            kCVPixelBufferMetalCompatibilityKey as String: true,
157	        ]
158	    }
159	
160	    /// Today's answers, stated: AVFoundation conforms every source to the
161	    /// composition's colour, so an SDR-only project keeps its pixels and
162	    /// labels. A composition holding an HLG, PQ or wide-gamut source is built
163	    /// with `ConvertingCompositor` instead (`Compositor+Input.swift`, spec
164	    /// §11 GR-15 as amended), which answers both true and runs step 0.
165	    var canConformColorOfSourceFrames: Bool { false }
166	    /// False here; true in `ConvertingCompositor` (see above).
167	    var supportsHDRSourceFrames: Bool { false }
168	
169	    var requiredPixelBufferAttributesForRenderContext: [String: any Sendable] {
170	        [
171	            kCVPixelBufferPixelFormatTypeKey as String: Int(Compositor.outputPixelFormat),
172	            kCVPixelBufferMetalCompatibilityKey as String: true,
173	        ]
174	    }
175	
176	    /// A new context means new pixel buffers, so every `CVMetalTexture`
177	    /// wrapping a buffer from the OLD context is stale — the cache is flushed
178	    /// rather than left to age out, because those textures pin IOSurfaces the
179	    /// old context is trying to release.
180	    func renderContextChanged(_ newRenderContext: AVVideoCompositionRenderContext) {
181	        lock.lock()
182	        renderContext = newRenderContext
183	        lock.unlock()
184	        renderer?.flushPixelBufferTextures()
185	    }
186	
187	    func startRequest(_ asyncVideoCompositionRequest: AVAsynchronousVideoCompositionRequest) {
188	        renderQueue.async { [weak self] in
189	            guard let self = self else {
190	                asyncVideoCompositionRequest.finishCancelledRequest()
191	                return
192	            }
193	            guard !self.isCancelled else {
194	                asyncVideoCompositionRequest.finishCancelledRequest()
195	                return
196	            }
197	            self.serve(asyncVideoCompositionRequest)
198	        }
199	    }
200	
201	    /// Flushes the queue: the cancelled flag makes every request already
202	    /// queued answer `finishCancelledRequest`, and the empty `sync` waits for
203	    /// the one in flight. AVFoundation calls this on a seek and at teardown,
204	    /// and requires that no request be left unanswered.
205	    func cancelAllPendingVideoCompositionRequests() {
206	        setCancelled(true)
207	        renderQueue.sync {}
208	        setCancelled(false)
209	    }
210	
211	    // MARK: - Serving one frame
212	
213	    private func serve(_ request: AVAsynchronousVideoCompositionRequest) {
214	        let started = CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent()
215	        guard let renderer = renderer else {
216	            request.finish(with: CompositorError.metalUnavailable)
217	            return
218	        }
219	        guard let destination = request.renderContext.newPixelBuffer() else {
220	            request.finish(with: CompositorError.noPixelBuffer)
221	            return
222	        }
223	        let instruction = request.videoCompositionInstruction as? RecipeInstruction
224	        let key = instruction?.recipeKey ?? 0
225	        let ticks = CompositionBuilder.ticks(request.compositionTime)
226	        // A playing preview's prefetch follows the frame asked for (G-36 (d)).
227	        GraphicPrefetch.shared.reach(key, ticks: ticks)
228	        // The key is the whole ask: `RecipeSource.recipe(for:at:)` reads the
229	        // project AND that key's `RecipeOptions` under one hold, so a burn-in
230	        // an export asked for arrives here without this file, the
231	        // instruction or `CompositionBuilder` carrying a flag of its own
232	        // (spec §7.3). Do not read the two halves separately.
233	        let recipe = RecipeSource.shared.recipe(for: key, at: ticks)
234	        do {
235	            try renderer.render(
236	                recipe: recipe, into: destination, request: request, instruction: instruction,
237	                converts: canConformColorOfSourceFrames)
238	            request.finish(withComposedVideoFrame: destination)
239	            #if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
240	            PlaybackTrials.shared.served(
241	                key, ticks: ticks, seconds: CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent() - started,
242	                buffer: destination)
243	            #endif
244	            WaveformTaps.shared.offer(
245	                destination, key: instruction?.recipeKey ?? 0,
246	                signal: ScopeSignal(canvas: recipe?.canvas))
247	        } catch {
248	            // A frame that will not compose is dropped: the player shows the last one.
249	            request.finish(with: error)
250	        }
251	        record(CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent() - started)
252	    }
253	
254	    // MARK: - Timing log
255	
256	    /// Averages over a two-second window (120 frames) and reports the worst
257	    /// frame in it, which is the number that matters — an 8 ms budget with a
258	    /// 40 ms outlier every second still stutters (§7.5).
259	    private func record(_ seconds: Double) {
260	        guard Compositor.timingEnabled else { return }
261	        lock.lock()
262	        frames += 1
263	        totalSeconds += seconds
264	        worstSeconds = max(worstSeconds, seconds)
265	        let due = frames >= 120
266	        let average = totalSeconds / Double(max(frames, 1)) * 1000
267	        let worst = worstSeconds * 1000
268	        if due {
269	            frames = 0
270	            totalSeconds = 0
271	            worstSeconds = 0
272	        }
273	        lock.unlock()
274	        if due {
275	            // Step 0's passes over the same window (spec §11 GR-15): 0 for a
276	            // frame with no converted source. Appended, so the line's prefix
277	            // stays what the proofs' timing pattern reads.
278	            let passes = renderer?.inputs.takePassCount() ?? 0
279	            NSLog("[framejob] compositor: %.2f ms average, %.2f ms worst over 120 frames, "
280	                + "%ld input passes", average, worst, passes)
281	        }
282	    }
283	
284	    private var isCancelled: Bool {
285	        lock.lock()
286	        defer { lock.unlock() }
287	        return cancelled
288	    }
289	
290	    private func setCancelled(_ value: Bool) {
291	        lock.lock()
292	        cancelled = value
293	        lock.unlock()
294	    }
295	}

3	/// The sheet that stays up for the write itself: a bar, a Cancel that really
4	/// stops the session, and — once the file lands — the result and a Show in
5	/// Finder (spec §10 step 10).
6	///
7	/// It owns the `Exporter`, which is why the export survives everything the
8	/// editor does next: the sheet is retained by the presenting controller for
9	/// as long as it is on screen, and nothing else holds the session.
10	///
11	/// Its own file rather than the foot of `ExportSheetController.swift`, which
12	/// stood at 1114 lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap. The seam is where
13	/// the two sheets stop having anything in common: the settings card is a
14	/// conversation with the core — every number it shows comes back from
15	/// `rc_export_settings`, and its controls only decide what to ask for — and
16	/// this one has already finished asking. It holds a project handle, a URL and
17	/// an `Exporter`, watches one number climb, and turns into its own result
18	/// panel; nothing on it can change what is being written.
19	///
20	/// Being a separate CLASS is what makes the cut free. `private` on an
21	/// extension member reaches only its own file, so splitting a type across
22	/// files costs every crossing member its privacy — the price
23	/// `ExporterLoudness.swift` records paying, and the price the two `extension
24	/// ExportSheetController` files beside this one pay. A type carries its own
25	/// scope, so every member below keeps the visibility it had, and
26	/// `EditorViewController+Export.swift` presenting it is the only name that
27	/// crosses.
28	final class ExportProgressSheetController: NSViewController {
29	    private let exporter = Exporter()
30	    /// The project handle as the export was confirmed. Handles are immutable
31	    /// (spec §5.5), so edits made after this point cannot reach the file.
32	    private let project: ReelProject
33	    private let urls: [UInt32: URL]
34	    private let settings: ExportSettings
35	    private let destination: URL
36	    /// What the export asks of the RECIPE rather than of the settings — the
37	    /// timecode burn-in (spec §7.3, road map 2's phase 7). It is a separate
38	    /// argument because it is a separate question: `ExportSettings` is what
39	    /// `rc_export_settings` resolved, and an option posted through the
40	    /// override table would be dropped in silence and the file reported a
41	    /// success. Defaulted, so a caller that does not burn in is written the
42	    /// way it always was.
43	    private let options: RecipeOptions
44	    /// The document's compiled graphics as the export was confirmed (G-13),
45	    /// pinned by `Exporter.export` for the write.
46	    private let graphics: GraphicSet?
47	
48	    private let bar = NSProgressIndicator()
49	    private let statusLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "Preparing…")
50	    private let percentLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: "0 %")
51	    /// Set in `loadView`; the only implicitly-unwrapped optionals the file has
52	    /// (app/CLAUDE.md allows them for exactly this).
53	    private var stopButton: NSButton!
54	    private var revealButton: NSButton!
55	
56	    private var didStart = false
57	    private var didFinish = false
58	    /// This export's booking in the encoder ledger (spec §11 CX-18): counted, never held —
59	    /// a person who chose Export… asked to write now. nil on an AVFoundation row and once
60	    /// it is over.
61	    private var ledgerToken: UInt64?
62	
63	    init(
64	        project: ReelProject, urls: [UInt32: URL], settings: ExportSettings, to url: URL,
65	        options: RecipeOptions = .none, graphics: GraphicSet? = nil
66	    ) {
67	        self.project = project
68	        self.urls = urls
69	        self.settings = settings
70	        self.destination = url
71	        self.options = options
72	        self.graphics = graphics
73	        super.init(nibName: nil, bundle: nil)
74	    }
75	
76	    @available(*, unavailable)
77	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
78	        fatalError("ExportProgressSheetController does not support NSCoder")
79	    }
80	
81	    deinit {
82	        let token = ledgerToken
83	        ledgerToken = nil
84	        ExportEncoderLedger.shared.end(token)
85	    }
86	
87	    override func loadView() {
88	        styleSheetProgressBar(bar)
89	
90	        styleSheetStatusLabel(statusLabel)
91	        statusLabel.stringValue = "Preparing “\(destination.lastPathComponent)”…"
92	
93	        percentLabel.font = DS.mono(11)
94	        percentLabel.textColor = DS.textFaint
95	
96	        let content = makeProgressStack([bar, statusLabel, percentLabel])
97	
98	        stopButton = StickerButton(
99	            title: "Cancel", style: .secondary, target: self, action: #selector(stopClicked(_:)))
100	        revealButton = StickerButton(
101	            title: "Show in Finder", style: .primary, target: self,
102	            action: #selector(revealClicked(_:)))
103	        hideReturnTarget(revealButton)
104	
105	        view = makeSheetView(
106	            title: "Exporting",
107	            content: content,
108	            buttonRow: makeButtonRow(cancel: stopButton, apply: revealButton))
109	    }
110	
111	    override func viewDidAppear() {
112	        super.viewDidAppear()
113	        guard !didStart else { return }
114	        didStart = true
115	        // Booked BEFORE `export`, whose early refusals finish synchronously inside it.
116	        ledgerToken = ExportEncoderLedger.shared.begin(settings)
117	        exporter.export(
118	            project: project, urls: urls, settings: settings, to: destination, options: options,
119	            graphics: graphics,
120	            progress: { [weak self] value in self?.progressed(value) },
121	            completion: { [weak self] result in self?.finished(result) })
122	    }
123	
124	    // MARK: - Exporter callbacks
125	
126	    private func progressed(_ value: Double) {
127	        guard !didFinish else { return }
128	        let clamped = min(max(value, 0), 1)
129	        bar.doubleValue = clamped
130	        percentLabel.stringValue = "\(Int((clamped * 100).rounded())) %"
131	        // The exporter names its own phase while it has one. Without this the
132	        // label would claim to be writing a file during the loudness
133	        // measurement — which on an audio-only export is half the wait, and
134	        // the half where nothing is on disk yet.
135	        if let phase = exporter.phaseDescription {
136	            statusLabel.stringValue = phase
137	        } else if clamped > 0 {
138	            statusLabel.stringValue = "Writing “\(destination.lastPathComponent)”…"
139	        }
140	    }
141	
142	    /// The one exit for all three outcomes. Cancelling closes the sheet and
143	    /// removes the half-written file; success and failure both turn the sheet
144	    /// into its own result panel rather than trading it for an alert.
145	    private func finished(_ result: Result<URL, any Error>) {
146	        didFinish = true
147	        // Cleared before `end`, whose post may launch a held queue job.
148	        let token = ledgerToken
149	        ledgerToken = nil
150	        ExportEncoderLedger.shared.end(token)
151	        stopButton.isEnabled = true
152	        switch result {
153	        case .success(let url):
154	            bar.doubleValue = 1
155	            percentLabel.stringValue = "100 %"
156	            // What the file actually holds, normalised or not: the export
157	            // measured its own mix on the way through, so the numbers are a
158	            // report rather than a promise.
159	            let measured = exporter.loudnessReport.map { " \($0.summary)." } ?? ""
160	            // What the graphics warned while the file was drawn: a count on
161	            // the line, the list in its tooltip (G-24 (c)).
162	            let warnings = exporter.graphicWarnings
163	            statusLabel.stringValue = "Exported “\(url.lastPathComponent)”.\(measured)"
164	                + Exporter.graphicWarningSuffix(warnings)
165	            statusLabel.toolTip = Exporter.graphicWarningDetails(warnings)
166	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
167	            stopButton.title = "Close"
168	            revealButton.isHidden = false
169	            revealButton.isEnabled = true
170	        case .failure(let error):
171	            if case Exporter.ExportError.cancelled = error {
172	                try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination)
173	                dismiss(self)
174	                return
175	            }
176	            bar.doubleValue = 0
177	            percentLabel.stringValue = ""
178	            statusLabel.stringValue = error.localizedDescription
179	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
180	            stopButton.title = "Close"
181	        }
182	    }
183	
184	    // MARK: - Buttons
185	
186	    /// Cancel while it runs, Close once it is over. One button because there
187	    /// is only ever one thing to do with a sheet that is busy.
188	    @objc private func stopClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
189	        guard !didFinish else {
190	            dismiss(self)
191	            return
192	        }
193	        stopButton.isEnabled = false
194	        statusLabel.stringValue = "Stopping…"
195	        exporter.cancel()
196	    }
197	
198	    @objc private func revealClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
199	        guard didFinish else { return }
200	        NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([destination])
201	        dismiss(self)
202	    }
203	}

3	// MARK: - The dev-tools seam: tools compiled only under FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
4	
5	/// Where the dev tools live (road map 11, spec §11 V-1 and V-2).
6	///
7	/// **The flag.** `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` is a Swift compilation condition that
8	/// Debug and Release set and the Distribution configuration does not
9	/// (`project.yml`), so every proof and agent session, which launch Release,
10	/// has the dev tools and the binary `make dist` builds has none of their
11	/// code (V-1). A dev tool is an ORDINARY tool (V-2): a handler in
12	/// `devHandlers`, a row from `devTools()`, and nothing else — the parity
13	/// check, the argument gate and the schema checks cover it as they cover a
14	/// product tool, in both builds, because both tables are merged before any
15	/// of them reads.
16	///
17	/// **Why the check greps a marker, not tool names.** Swift string literals
18	/// of 15 UTF-8 bytes or fewer are stored inline in the code of an `-O`
19	/// binary, not as contiguous bytes, so a short tool name such as
20	/// `snapshot_ui` (11) can never be found in either build and an absence
21	/// check on it would pass for nothing. `tools/proof/dist_check.py` reads
22	/// `devToolsMarker` out of this file instead — at least 16 bytes — and
23	/// requires it present in Release's binary and absent from Distribution's.
24	///
25	/// **What keeps the marker live.** The flag-on `devTools()` logs it, so the
26	/// optimiser cannot drop the literal. V2 adds rows and handlers here with no
27	/// edit to the check.
28	///
29	/// **Where the rows go.** `catalogJSON()` splices `devTools()` in
30	/// immediately BEFORE the file tools, never at the end: the catalog's last
31	/// eleven names are the file group plus `record_screen`, which
32	/// `recording_probe.py` asserts. Swift takes no `#if` inside a dictionary
33	/// literal, so `AgentServer.swift` merges `devHandlers` through
34	/// `withDevHandlers` and `devOffMainTools` by a union, one line each.
35	extension AgentServer {
36	    typealias ToolHandler = (AgentServer) -> ([String: Any]) throws -> String
37	
38	    /// `product` with `devHandlers` merged in. A dev tool that reuses a
39	    /// product tool's name keeps the PRODUCT handler and complains the way
40	    /// the startup parity check does.
41	    static func withDevHandlers(_ product: [String: ToolHandler]) -> [String: ToolHandler] {
42	        var merged = product
43	        for (name, handler) in devHandlers.sorted(by: { $0.key < $1.key }) {
44	            if merged[name] != nil {
45	                let msg = "dev tool \(name) reuses a product tool's name"
46	                assertionFailure(msg)
47	                NSLog("Frame Job: %@", msg)
48	                continue
49	            }
50	            merged[name] = handler
51	        }
52	        return merged
53	    }
54	
55	    /// Every dev tool's name, in either build (empty in Distribution): the
56	    /// assistant withholds each one (spec §11 AI-7, `AssistantToolTable`).
57	    static var devToolNames: Set<String> { Set(devHandlers.keys) }
58	
59	    #if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
60	    // dist_check.py parses the next line (D1) and requires it bare — nothing after the
61	    // closing quote — at least 16 bytes, present in Release's binary, absent from Distribution's.
62	    static let devToolsMarker = "framejob-dev-tools-compiled-in"
63	
64	    private static let devHandlers: [String: ToolHandler] = [
65	        // AgentServer+Snapshot.swift
66	        "snapshot_ui": { $0.snapshotUI },
67	        // AgentServer+MenuItem.swift
68	        "perform_menu_item": { $0.performMenuItem },
69	        "cancel_sheet": { $0.cancelSheet },
70	        // AgentServer+InspectorTab.swift
71	        "select_inspector_tab": { $0.selectInspectorTab },
72	        // AgentServer+Assistant.swift
73	        "assistant_send": { $0.assistantSend },
74	        "assistant_answer": { $0.assistantAnswer },
75	        // AgentServer+PlayPreview.swift
76	        "play_preview": { $0.playPreview },
77	        // AgentServer+GraphicMemory.swift
78	        "graphic_memory": { $0.graphicMemory },
79	    ]
80	
81	    static let devOffMainTools: Set<String> = [
82	        "snapshot_ui", "perform_menu_item", "cancel_sheet", "assistant_send", "assistant_answer",
83	        "play_preview", "graphic_memory",
84	    ]
85	
86	    /// The dev tools' catalog rows, in catalog order: `snapshot_ui` (V2a),
87	    /// `perform_menu_item` and `cancel_sheet` (V2b), `select_inspector_tab`
88	    /// (V3), `assistant_send` and `assistant_answer` (road map 12 A1),
89	    /// `play_preview` (issue #127, G-36), `graphic_memory` (issue #127,
90	    /// G-37). The log is what keeps `devToolsMarker` in the optimised binary;
91	    /// it never says `Frame Job: `, the prefix a proof reads as the parity
92	    /// check complaining.
93	    func devTools() -> [[String: Any]] {
94	        let rows: [[String: Any]] = [
95	            snapshotUITool(), performMenuItemTool(), cancelSheetTool(), selectInspectorTabTool(),
96	            assistantSendTool(), assistantAnswerTool(), playPreviewTool(), graphicMemoryTool(),
97	        ]
98	        NSLog("Frame Job agent server: %@, %ld dev tools", Self.devToolsMarker, rows.count)
99	        return rows
100	    }
101	    #else
102	    private static let devHandlers: [String: ToolHandler] = [:]
103	
104	    static let devOffMainTools: Set<String> = []
105	
106	    /// Distribution ships no dev tools.
107	    func devTools() -> [[String: Any]] {
108	        []
109	    }
110	    #endif
111	}
