3	/// The export queue (road map 2's phase 7e): the exports a person has
4	/// confirmed but does not want to sit and watch, run one after another while
5	/// the editor stays live.
6	///
7	/// **There is no AppKit in this file, and that is the design rather than
8	/// tidiness.** A queue window can be checked by neither of this project's two
9	/// instruments: the offscreen harness renders an `EditorViewController` into a
10	/// window and nothing else, and MCP drives the app through tools — and the
11	/// agent's `export` enqueues here, so a tool reaches this list but never the
12	/// window (below, spec §11 #326). What a proof CAN do is
13	/// compile a probe out of the whole of `app/Sources`
14	/// (`tools/proof/phase6_chrome.py`'s `build_probe`), make one of these,
15	/// enqueue two jobs, spin the main run loop until `isIdle` and read `jobs`
16	/// back — without an `NSWindow` ever being ordered front. So the job list and
17	/// its state machine live here, where a script can reach them, and
18	/// `ExportQueueWindowController.swift` is a READER of this and nothing else:
19	/// it holds no job, decides nothing, and closing it stops nothing.
20	/// `AudioNormalize.swift` and `CaptionLayout.swift` are the same split — the
21	/// arithmetic where a script can call it, the dialog around it — and phase 5's
22	/// level meter is the closest sibling, where the MODEL publishes a number
23	/// precisely so that a proof need not photograph a window.
24	///
25	/// **The agent's `export` is a job here (spec §11 #326).** It keeps its
26	/// refusals synchronous, then enqueues exactly as Add to Queue does and
27	/// answers the job's id at once; `export_status` follows the job and
28	/// `cancel_export` calls `cancel` (`AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`). The
29	/// queue's own API is unchanged by it: the mirror reads `job(_:)` and
30	/// observes `didChangeNotification` like the window does, and no tool
31	/// exists for a person's own queued job.
32	///
33	/// **One job at a time, on the MAIN thread, a fresh `Exporter` for each.**
34	/// `Exporter.export`'s own doc says main-thread-only and one export at a time,
35	/// and it means both: it schedules a run-loop `Timer` — which must be
36	/// invalidated on the thread it was scheduled on — and calls its progress and
37	/// completion handlers on the main thread. So this is a CHAIN and not a pool:
38	/// `start()` runs the head of the list and each completion runs the next. A
39	/// `DispatchQueue` of exporters would be the wrong shape whatever the machine's
40	/// core count, and not only because of the timer — an `Exporter` carries
41	/// per-export state (`recipeKey`, `cancelRequested`, the loudness scratch
42	/// buffer), which is why each job gets its own rather than one being reset
43	/// between jobs. Every method below is main-thread-only for that reason, like
44	/// the exporter it drives.
45	///
46	/// **What a job holds is the whole of what it will write, captured when it was
47	/// confirmed.** The `ReelProject` is a handle and handles are immutable (spec
48	/// §5.5) — every edit and every undo makes a NEW one — so a queued write cannot
49	/// be reached by an edit made after it, and it needs no clone: `Exporter.export`
50	/// publishes it on a `RecipeSource` key it mints for itself, never the
51	/// document's, so even the frames the compositor serves this export come from
52	/// this handle. The document may be edited, undone or CLOSED while the job
53	/// waits; the handle is retained here and the Rust project behind it lives
54	/// until the job is gone.
55	///
56	/// **And the media URLs are resolved at ENQUEUE, which is what makes them part
57	/// of that same snapshot.** `ProjectDocument.mediaURLs()` resolves a bookmark
58	/// and asks the filesystem whether the file is there (`mediaURL(for:)`), so it
59	/// is a reading of the disk at the moment it is called: resolving at RUN time
60	/// would silently pick up a Relink… or a moved file from after the job was
61	/// queued, which is the exact change an immutable job exists to exclude. That
62	/// rule is structural here rather than remembered — `enqueue` takes a
63	/// `[UInt32: URL]` and a job holds no document, so there is nothing to ask
64	/// again later even if somebody wanted to.
65	///
66	/// **The REVERSE resolution is the third thing in that snapshot, and it was
67	/// missing.** Handle immutability covers the project and nothing beside it:
68	/// which clips play from a pre-rendered backwards file is a reading of the
69	/// disk too (`ProjectDocument.reverseState`, `ReverseCache.existing`), it
70	/// cannot be derived from a bare handle, and it lives in a side table keyed by
71	/// object IDENTITY — which the document overwrites on every edit and removes
72	/// when it closes. So a job queued from a timeline holding a reversed clip
73	/// used to answer `.none` the moment anything was edited, and `.none` means
74	/// "not reversed": the export took the forward asset at the mirrored source
75	/// window, unslated and unreported. It is captured here at enqueue, exactly as
76	/// the URLs are, and PINNED to this job's own handle for the length of its
77	/// write (`ReverseSource.pin`). Anything else the picture depends on that is
78	/// neither in the handle nor derivable from it joins that list.
79	///
80	/// **A bundled-encoder job also waits for memory (spec §11 CX-18).** An AV1 or VP9 job
81	/// starts only while `ExportEncoderLedger` admits it: nothing else booked, or the running
82	/// encoder exports — an Export… sheet's beside this queue's — fitting with it in a quarter
83	/// of physical memory. A held job says why in its `message` and is PASSED OVER by a later
84	/// job the ledger admits, an AVFoundation job always; the chain stays one job at a time.
85	/// The running job is booked from just before its `export` call to its finish, and a
86	/// booking's end — the queue's own or a sheet's — re-runs `start()` through the ledger's
87	/// notification.
88	final class ExportQueueController {
89	    /// The app's one queue: the export sheet's Add to Queue fills it and
90	    /// Window ▸ Export Queue shows it.
91	    static let shared = ExportQueueController()
92	
93	    /// Where a job is. A closed set with no associated values, so the two
94	    /// readers ask it different questions without either having to spell a
95	    /// message: the window's row draws its own wording (which carries a
96	    /// percentage the state cannot know), and a probe compares the case and
97	    /// reads `Job.message` for the sentence. The raw values are the same
98	    /// strings a probe writes into its JSON answer.
99	    enum State: String {
100	        /// Queued and not started. The only state a job can be enqueued in.
101	        case waiting
102	        /// The one job an `Exporter` is running. At most one at any moment.
103	        case running
104	        /// The file landed.
105	        case completed
106	        /// Stopped by a person, either before it started or mid-write — in
107	        /// which case its half-written file has been removed.
108	        case cancelled
109	        /// The exporter refused or failed. Whatever it had written is LEFT on
110	        /// disk, which is `ExportProgressSheetController`'s posture and not a
111	        /// new one: a cancel is a person saying "not this", where a failure is
112	        /// evidence, and the file names itself in the message.
113	        case failed
114	
115	        /// Whether the job is over, however it ended — the test for "may be
116	        /// removed from the list" and for "no longer holds a project handle
117	        /// worth keeping".
118	        var isFinished: Bool { self == .completed || self == .cancelled || self == .failed }
119	    }
120	
121	    /// One confirmed export. Everything it needs was read when it was
122	    /// enqueued; see the type doc for why that is the whole point of it.
123	    struct Job {
124	        /// Monotonic within one launch. The window's rows and every method
125	        /// below address a job by this rather than by index, because a job can
126	        /// be removed from the middle of the list while a later one runs.
127	        let id: UInt64
128	        /// The timeline as it was confirmed — immutable, and retained here, so
129	        /// the document behind it may be edited, undone or closed.
130	        ///
131	        /// A FINISHED job goes on holding it, and that is a real cost stated
132	        /// rather than hidden: a handle is the project's model and not its
133	        /// media, so it is JSON-sized, and Clear Finished (or Remove) is what
134	        /// releases it along with the row that says where the file went.
135	        /// Dropping the handle at the finish would buy those bytes back and
136	        /// cost the field its `let` — an immutable job whose contents change
137	        /// once is a harder thing to reason about than a list somebody tidies.
138	        let project: ReelProject
139	        /// The media files as they resolved AT ENQUEUE.
140	        let urls: [UInt32: URL]
141	        /// Which of this timeline's clips play from a pre-rendered backwards
142	        /// file, as that resolved AT ENQUEUE — the type doc's third piece of
143	        /// the snapshot. Read from `ReverseSource` here and published back to
144	        /// it under this job's own handle while the job runs, because the
145	        /// document's copy is overwritten by the next edit and dropped when it
146	        /// closes.
147	        let reverse: ReverseResolution
148	        let settings: ExportSettings
149	        let destination: URL
150	        /// What this export asks of the PICTURE besides the timeline — the
151	        /// burn-in (`RecipeOptions`). Carried per job, because two jobs from
152	        /// one document may legitimately differ in it.
153	        let options: RecipeOptions
154	        /// The document's compiled graphics as they stood AT ENQUEUE (G-13) —
155	        /// the type doc's list again: a module saved after Add to Queue is not
156	        /// in the handle, and the document's set is swapped by that save and
157	        /// dropped when it closes. `Exporter.export` pins it for the write.
158	        let graphics: GraphicSet?
159	        var state: State = .waiting
160	        /// 0…1, and only meaningful while `state` is `.running`.
161	        var progress: Double = 0
162	        /// The line a person reads when it is over: what was written and what
163	        /// the file measured, or why it stopped — plus the one thing worth
164	        /// saying mid-flight, that a cancel is in hand. While it waits, the
165	        /// ledger's sentence when the memory limit holds it (CX-18), else nil.
166	        var message: String?
167	        /// What the exporter says it is doing right now, or nil for "writing",
168	        /// which is the caller's own wording. Today the only phase is the
169	        /// loudness measurement, which on an audio-only export is half the wait
170	        /// and the half where nothing is on disk yet.
171	        ///
172	        /// A field of its own rather than a use of `message`, because the two
173	        /// are written by different things at the same time: the progress tick
174	        /// arrives ten times a second and would otherwise wipe the "Stopping…"
175	        /// a person had just asked for.
176	        var phase: String?
177	        /// Set on a COMPLETED job when a later job starts writing to the same
178	        /// path, because from that moment this row's file is not this row's
179	        /// any more — `Exporter.startWriting` removes whatever is at the
180	        /// destination before it builds its pipeline, so the earlier export is
181	        /// gone whether the later one succeeds, fails or is cancelled.
182	        ///
183	        /// The row stops claiming "Exported …" and stops offering Show in
184	        /// Finder. It is a fact about what happened rather than a state: the
185	        /// job really did complete, and rewriting its `state` would lose that.
186	        ///
187	        /// One case marks it where the file in fact survives, and it is the
188	        /// honest direction of the two: a later job whose COMPOSITION fails to
189	        /// build returns before the delete, so nothing was destroyed. It is
190	        /// left alone rather than reached for, because knowing which failures
191	        /// precede the delete means reading `Exporter`'s stages from here, and
192	        /// a shared destination implies a shared project — a build that failed
193	        /// for job 2 would almost always have failed for job 1.
194	        var superseded: Bool = false
195	        /// What the graphics warned while a COMPLETED job's file was drawn
196	        /// (G-24 (c)): the row's count and its tooltip's list.
197	        var graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning] = []
198	        /// What a COMPLETED job's sound measured, read off its exporter at the
199	        /// finish — the figures the row's message summarises, kept whole for
200	        /// `export_status`'s `loudness` (spec §11 #326). nil otherwise.
201	        var loudness: ExportLoudness? = nil
202	
203	        /// What the row calls this job. The file name and not the path: the
204	        /// row is narrow, and the full path is the tooltip's job.
205	        var name: String { destination.lastPathComponent }
206	    }
207	
208	    /// Posted after any change to `jobs` — an enqueue, a progress tick, a
209	    /// finish, a cancel, a removal — with the controller as the `object`, so
210	    /// an observer of the shared queue is never woken by a probe's own
211	    /// instance. Main thread, like everything else here.
212	    static let didChangeNotification = Notification.Name(
213	        "com.kgalligan.framejob.exportQueueDidChange")
214	
215	    /// Every job this launch still knows about, in the order they were added.
216	    /// A finished one stays until it is removed, because "it is done and here
217	    /// is where it went" is the queue's other job.
218	    private(set) var jobs: [Job] = []
219	
220	    /// The exporter running `runningID`'s job, and nil whenever nothing is
221	    /// running. Set and cleared together with the job's state, so `isIdle` can
222	    /// be answered from `jobs` alone.
223	    private var exporter: Exporter?
224	
225	    /// The handle whose reverse resolution is pinned in `ReverseSource` right
226	    /// now — the running job's, and nil whenever nothing is running. Held
227	    /// separately from the job so that `launch` and `finished` are provably one
228	    /// pin and one release, whatever happens to the list in between.
229	    private var pinnedProject: ReelProject?
230	
231	    /// The running job's booking in the encoder ledger (CX-18), nil whenever nothing runs
232	    /// or the running job is an AVFoundation one. Taken BEFORE `end` in `finished`: the
233	    /// ledger's post can launch — and book — the next job inside that call.
234	    private var ledgerToken: UInt64?
235	
236	    private let ledger = ExportEncoderLedger.shared
237	
238	    /// True only while `start()` is inside `Exporter.export`. An early refusal
239	    /// — `noPlan`, `emptyTimeline` — completes SYNCHRONOUSLY, so `finished`
240	    /// can run before `export` has returned; without this flag the next job
241	    /// would be launched from inside the previous one's stack frame and a
242	    /// queue of refusals would recurse as deep as it is long. With it, a
243	    /// re-entrant `start()` is refused and the frame already on the stack
244	    /// picks the next job up in its own loop.
245	    private var isLaunching = false
246	
247	    private var nextID: UInt64 = 1
248	
249	    /// Internal rather than private, and deliberately: a proof compiles a
250	    /// probe out of `app/Sources` and makes its OWN queue, so that running two
251	    /// jobs in a script cannot disturb — or be disturbed by — the app's shared
252	    /// one. It is the same reason `ExportPresetsStore` is a value a test can
253	    /// make.
254	    init() {
255	        // A booking's end — a sheet's as much as this queue's — may admit a held job.
256	        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
257	            self, selector: #selector(ledgerChanged(_:)),
258	            name: ExportEncoderLedger.didChangeNotification, object: ledger)
259	    }
260	
261	    @objc private func ledgerChanged(_ note: Notification) { start() }
262	
263	    @available(*, unavailable)
264	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
265	        fatalError("ExportQueueController does not support NSCoder")
266	    }
267	
268	    // MARK: - Asking
269	
270	    /// Nothing waiting and nothing running. The queue's own "are we there
271	    /// yet", and what a probe spins the run loop until.
272	    ///
273	    /// Answered from `jobs` rather than from `exporter`, so it means the same
274	    /// thing to a caller that cannot see the private state.
275	    var isIdle: Bool {
276	        !jobs.contains { $0.state == .waiting || $0.state == .running }
277	    }
278	
279	    /// The job an exporter is writing right now, if any.
280	    var runningJob: Job? { jobs.first { $0.state == .running } }
281	
282	    /// How many are still queued behind it.
283	    var waitingCount: Int { jobs.filter { $0.state == .waiting }.count }
284	
285	    func job(_ id: UInt64) -> Job? { jobs.first { $0.id == id } }
286	
287	    // MARK: - Filling
288	
289	    /// Adds one confirmed export and starts the queue if it is not already
290	    /// running. Answers the job's id, so a caller can follow it.
291	    ///
292	    /// The arguments are `Exporter.export`'s, and that is not a coincidence:
293	    /// a job is exactly the call that will be made, held until its turn. Both
294	    /// `project` and `urls` are read by the CALLER, at the moment the save
295	    /// panel answered (`EditorViewController.enqueueExport`), which is what
296	    /// the type doc means by capturing at enqueue.
297	    ///
298	    /// **Two jobs may name one file, and the queue still does not refuse it —
299	    /// but it no longer pretends the person was warned.** The reason first
300	    /// given here was that "the save panel asked about replacing an existing
301	    /// file both times", and that is false in exactly the case that matters:
302	    /// `NSSavePanel` prompts only when something is at the path as Save is
303	    /// confirmed, and job 1 spends its build and its whole loudness
304	    /// measurement pass with nothing at the destination — `Exporter.export`
305	    /// does both before `startWriting` deletes and `AVAssetWriter` creates —
306	    /// so two Add to Queue actions in quick succession are never asked
307	    /// anything. Refusing here would still be wrong: overwriting your own
308	    /// export is a thing a person is allowed to do, and the queue must not be
309	    /// the one place in the app where they may not. What was wrong was the
310	    /// silence AFTERWARDS, and `launch` is where that is answered — the
311	    /// earlier row is marked `superseded` the moment a later job starts
312	    /// writing to its path, so no row goes on offering a file that another
313	    /// job has since deleted or replaced.
314	    @discardableResult
315	    func enqueue(
316	        project: ReelProject, urls: [UInt32: URL], settings: ExportSettings, to url: URL,
317	        options: RecipeOptions = .none, graphics: GraphicSet? = nil
318	    ) -> UInt64 {
319	        let id = nextID
320	        nextID += 1
321	        jobs.append(
322	            Job(
323	                id: id, project: project, urls: urls,
324	                // The third piece of the enqueue-time snapshot; the type doc
325	                // says why it cannot be left to be asked again at run time.
326	                reverse: ReverseSource.shared.resolution(publishedFor: project),
327	                settings: settings, destination: url, options: options, graphics: graphics))
328	        didChange()
329	        start()
330	        return id
331	    }
332	
333	    // MARK: - Running
334	
335	    /// Runs the first waiting job the encoder ledger admits, if nothing is
336	    /// running already — passing over a held one (CX-18 (7)). Idempotent
337	    /// and safe to call at any time: `enqueue` calls it, every completion
338	    /// calls it, the ledger's change calls it, and a caller may call it itself.
339	    ///
340	    /// The loop is for the synchronous-refusal case `isLaunching` describes: a
341	    /// job the exporter refuses without ever going asynchronous has already
342	    /// finished by the time `launch` returns, and this frame takes the next
343	    /// one rather than recursing into it.
344	    func start() {
345	        guard !isLaunching else { return }
346	        isLaunching = true
347	        defer { isLaunching = false }
348	        while exporter == nil, let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: {
349	            $0.state == .waiting && ledger.admits($0.settings)
350	        }) {
351	            launch(at: index)
352	        }
353	        noteHeld()
354	    }
355	
356	    /// Every waiting encoder job's `message` set to why it is held, or cleared when it is
357	    /// not — leaving out this queue's own running booking, which it waits behind anyway.
358	    private func noteHeld() {
359	        var changed = false
360	        for index in jobs.indices
361	        where jobs[index].state == .waiting && jobs[index].settings.writer != nil {
362	            let sentence = ledger.waitingSentence(for: jobs[index].settings, ignoring: ledgerToken)
363	            if jobs[index].message != sentence {
364	                jobs[index].message = sentence
365	                changed = true
366	            }
367	        }
368	        if changed { didChange() }
369	    }
370	
371	    /// One job handed to one fresh `Exporter`. The exporter is stored BEFORE
372	    /// the call, because an early refusal calls back before `export` returns
373	    /// and `finished` has to find it there.
374	    private func launch(at index: Int) {
375	        let job = jobs[index]
376	        jobs[index].state = .running
377	        jobs[index].progress = 0
378	        jobs[index].message = nil
379	        jobs[index].phase = nil
380	        // Any COMPLETED row naming this same path stops claiming its file
381	        // here, and here rather than when the file is actually deleted: the
382	        // delete happens inside `Exporter.startWriting`, seconds later and in
383	        // a file this one may not reach into, and being early is the honest
384	        // direction — a row that stops offering a file just before it is
385	        // destroyed costs a person nothing, where one that offers it just
386	        // after sends them to the Finder for something that is gone.
387	        for other in jobs.indices
388	        where other != index && jobs[other].state == .completed
389	            && jobs[other].destination == job.destination
390	        {
391	            jobs[other].superseded = true
392	        }
393	        // The job's own reverse resolution, held against its own handle for
394	        // exactly the length of this write. At most one pin exists at a time,
395	        // which is the invariant `ReverseSource.pin` asks its callers for and
396	        // which this class keeps for free by running one job at a time.
397	        ReverseSource.shared.pin(job.reverse, for: job.project)
398	        pinnedProject = job.project
399	        // Booked BEFORE `export`, whose early refusals finish synchronously inside it.
400	        ledgerToken = ledger.begin(job.settings)
401	        let exporter = Exporter()
402	        self.exporter = exporter
403	        didChange()
404	        exporter.export(
405	            project: job.project, urls: job.urls, settings: job.settings, to: job.destination,
406	            options: job.options, graphics: job.graphics,
407	            progress: { [weak self] value in self?.progressed(job.id, value) },
408	            completion: { [weak self] result in self?.finished(job.id, result) })
409	    }
410	
411	    private func progressed(_ id: UInt64, _ value: Double) {
412	        guard let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }),
413	            jobs[index].state == .running
414	        else { return }
415	        jobs[index].progress = min(max(value, 0), 1)
416	        // The exporter names its own phase while it has one. The progress
417	        // sheet asks the same question with the same call; a row that said
418	        // "Writing" through the measurement would be claiming a file that does
419	        // not exist yet.
420	        jobs[index].phase = exporter?.phaseDescription
421	        didChange()
422	    }
423	
424	    /// The one exit for all three outcomes, and the mirror of
425	    /// `ExportProgressSheetController.finished` — deliberately, because there
426	    /// must not be two accounts of what finishing an export means. The
427	    /// exporter is cleared first, so the `start()` at the foot can hand the
428	    /// next job a fresh one.
429	    private func finished(_ id: UInt64, _ result: Result<URL, any Error>) {
430	        // Read BEFORE the exporter is dropped: `Exporter.finish` publishes the
431	        // measurement and then calls this, so the report is there now and only
432	        // now.
433	        let report = exporter?.loudnessReport
434	        let measured = report.map { " \($0.summary)." } ?? ""
435	        let warnings = exporter?.graphicWarnings ?? []
436	        exporter = nil
437	        // The pin goes with the exporter, and from `pinnedProject` rather than
438	        // from the job, so that releasing it cannot depend on the job still
439	        // being in the list. Exactly one release per `launch`, which is what
440	        // `ReverseSource.pin` asks for; a pin left behind would retain the
441	        // Rust project for the life of the process.
442	        if let pinned = pinnedProject {
443	            ReverseSource.shared.unpin(pinned)
444	            pinnedProject = nil
445	        }
446	        if let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }) {
447	            jobs[index].phase = nil
448	            switch result {
449	            case .success(let url):
450	                jobs[index].state = .completed
451	                jobs[index].progress = 1
452	                jobs[index].graphicWarnings = warnings
453	                jobs[index].loudness = report
454	                // The count BEFORE the loudness figures: the row truncates
455	                // its tail (`ExportQueueRowView`).
456	                jobs[index].message = "Exported “\(url.lastPathComponent)”."
457	                    + Exporter.graphicWarningSuffix(warnings, hover: false) + measured
458	            case .failure(let error):
459	                if case Exporter.ExportError.cancelled = error {
460	                    // A cancelled job leaves nothing behind, and this line is
461	                    // DEFENCE IN DEPTH rather than the thing that achieves it
462	                    // — measured, because the obvious reading is wrong and a
463	                    // reader who believes it would be relying on a guarantee
464	                    // this line does not provide. Both pipelines already
465	                    // clean up after themselves: `AVAssetWriter.cancelWriting()`
466	                    // removes its own part-file (`ExporterWriter.swift` says
467	                    // so where it calls it) and `ImageSequenceWriter.report`
468	                    // removes its own. Deleting this line changes no observable
469	                    // outcome — phase 7's proof mutated it away and scored
470	                    // 77/77 — so the check beside it is written as the OUTCOME
471	                    // ("nothing is left behind") and not as a guard on this
472	                    // call. Keep it: it costs nothing, it states the policy
473	                    // where the policy is decided, and it is what holds if a
474	                    // third pipeline ever arrives that is less tidy.
475	                    // `ExportProgressSheetController.finished` is the same line
476	                    // for the same reason.
477	                    try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: jobs[index].destination)
478	                    jobs[index].state = .cancelled
479	                    jobs[index].progress = 0
480	                    jobs[index].message = "Cancelled."
481	                } else {
482	                    jobs[index].state = .failed
483	                    jobs[index].progress = 0
484	                    jobs[index].message = error.localizedDescription
485	                }
486	            }
487	        }
488	        didChange()
489	        // Cleared before `end`, whose post may launch and book the next job.
490	        let token = ledgerToken
491	        ledgerToken = nil
492	        ledger.end(token)
493	        start()
494	    }
495	
496	    // MARK: - Stopping and tidying
497	
498	    /// Stops one job, whether it has started or not.
499	    ///
500	    /// A WAITING job is simply marked: it has no exporter to stop and no file
501	    /// to remove, because nothing has been written under its name. A RUNNING
502	    /// one is asked to stop and answers through `finished`, which is where its
503	    /// file is removed — one exit, so a cancel from the window and a cancel
504	    /// from a script clean up identically. A finished job is left alone.
505	    func cancel(_ id: UInt64) {
506	        guard let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }) else { return }
507	        switch jobs[index].state {
508	        case .waiting:
509	            jobs[index].state = .cancelled
510	            jobs[index].message = "Cancelled before it started."
511	            didChange()
512	        case .running:
513	            jobs[index].message = "Stopping…"
514	            exporter?.cancel()
515	            didChange()
516	        case .completed, .cancelled, .failed:
517	            break
518	        }
519	    }
520	
521	    /// Stops everything. The WAITING jobs go first and the running one last,
522	    /// and the order is load-bearing: cancelling the running job posts its
523	    /// completion, and a completion starts the next waiting job — so stopping
524	    /// the writer first would start the very jobs this is meant to stop.
525	    func cancelAll() {
526	        for job in jobs where job.state == .waiting { cancel(job.id) }
527	        if let running = runningJob { cancel(running.id) }
528	    }
529	
530	    /// Drops one finished row. A job still waiting or running is not removed —
531	    /// cancel it first, which is what the window's one button does in its two
532	    /// states.
533	    func remove(_ id: UInt64) {
534	        guard let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }),
535	            jobs[index].state.isFinished
536	        else { return }
537	        jobs.remove(at: index)
538	        didChange()
539	    }
540	
541	    /// Drops every finished row and leaves the queue itself running.
542	    func clearFinished() {
543	        let before = jobs.count
544	        jobs.removeAll { $0.state.isFinished }
545	        if jobs.count != before { didChange() }
546	    }
547	
548	    private func didChange() {
549	        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: Self.didChangeNotification, object: self)
550	    }
551	}

2	// jobs and the sheet's time estimate, in process. `encoder_limit_proof.py` builds it as
3	// `main.swift` over every file in `app/Sources` but the app's own `main.swift`, on
4	// `swift_build.py`'s line, beside `Blank.mp4`, `Fonts` and a `default.metallib` of
5	// `Compositor.metal` and `ExportI010.metal`, and runs it:
6	//
7	//   encoder_limit_probe <AV.mov> <out folder> <answer.json>
8	//
9	// No app and no instance: the two live projects are built here from AV.mov, as
10	// `webm_readers_probe.swift` builds A1's — A1 (640 × 360, 30 fps, AV.mov from 0 under a
11	// two-second text clip) and W9 (1920 × 1080, AV.mov 24 times end to end at scale 3).
12	//
13	// The answer is RAW: the tables (P0), what the rule and the estimate answered (R, E), and
14	// what the live queue did (Q), each event stamped with a sequence number. The proof
15	// computes every expected value from P0's tables in its own arithmetic and scores the rows.
16	import AVFoundation
17	import AppKit
18	import Foundation
19	
20	DecoderSupport.enable()
21	NSApplication.shared.setActivationPolicy(.prohibited)
22	
23	let arguments = CommandLine.arguments
24	guard arguments.count == 4 else {
25	    print("usage: encoder_limit_probe <AV.mov> <out folder> <answer.json>")
26	    exit(2)
27	}
28	let media = URL(fileURLWithPath: arguments[1])
29	let outFolder = URL(fileURLWithPath: arguments[2], isDirectory: true)
30	let answerURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: arguments[3])
31	try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: outFolder, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
32	
33	let binaryDirectory = URL(fileURLWithPath: arguments[0]).deletingLastPathComponent()
34	    .standardizedFileURL
35	let fontsDirectory = binaryDirectory.appendingPathComponent("Fonts")
36	for name in (try? FileManager.default.contentsOfDirectory(atPath: fontsDirectory.path)) ?? []
37	where name.hasSuffix(".ttf") || name.hasSuffix(".otf") {
38	    CTFontManagerRegisterFontsForURL(
39	        fontsDirectory.appendingPathComponent(name) as CFURL, .process, nil)
40	}
41	
42	var answer: [String: Any] = [:]
43	func finish() -> Never {
44	    let data = (try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: answer, options: [.sortedKeys]))
45	        ?? Data("{}".utf8)
46	    try? data.write(to: answerURL)
47	    exit(0)
48	}

50	struct ProbeError: Error, CustomStringConvertible {
51	    let description: String
52	    init(_ d: String) { description = d }
53	}

55	// MARK: - P0: the tables
56	
57	func keyJSON(_ key: ExportEncoderKey) -> [String: Any] {
58	    ["preset": key.preset, "speed": key.speed?.rawValue ?? NSNull(), "bits": key.bits]
59	}

61	    ["at1080": f.at1080, "at2160": f.at2160, "source": f.source]
62	}
63	answer["pixels1080"] = ExportEncoderCosts.pixels1080
64	answer["pixels2160"] = ExportEncoderCosts.pixels2160
65	answer["memory"] = ExportEncoderCosts.memory.map { key, figure in
66	    ["key": keyJSON(key), "figure": figureJSON(figure)]
67	}
68	answer["time"] = ExportEncoderCosts.time.map { key, entry in
69	    ["key": keyJSON(key), "perFrame": figureJSON(entry.perFrame),
70	     "setupSeconds": entry.setupSeconds]
71	}

73	// MARK: - Synthetic settings
74	
75	/// Settings as the core would answer them for a row, decoded through the app's own type.
76	func settings(
77	    preset: String, writer: String?, speed: EncoderSpeed? = nil, color: String? = nil,
78	    width: Int, height: Int, frames: Int = 300, fps: [Int] = [30, 1]
79	) -> ExportSettings {
80	    var object: [String: Any] = [
81	        "preset": preset, "container": "mp4", "codec": preset, "width": width,
82	        "height": height, "fps": fps,
83	        "range": ["start": 0, "duration": frames * Int(Fps.thirty.frameDuration)],
84	    ]
85	    if let writer { object["writer"] = writer }
86	    if let speed { object["encoder_speed"] = speed.rawValue }
87	    if let color { object["color"] = color }
88	    let data = try! JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: object)
89	    return ReelJSON.decode(ExportSettings.self, from: String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self))!
90	}

92	/// One settings per measured key, by the proof's name for it.
93	func keyed(width: Int, height: Int, frames: Int = 300) -> [(String, ExportSettings)] {
94	    var out: [(String, ExportSettings)] = []
95	    for preset in ["av1", "av1_webm"] {
96	        for speed in EncoderSpeed.allCases {
97	            out.append(("\(preset):\(speed.rawValue)", settings(
98	                preset: preset, writer: "svt_av1", speed: speed, width: width, height: height,
99	                frames: frames)))
100	        }
101	    }
102	    out.append(("vp9_webm:sdr", settings(
103	        preset: "vp9_webm", writer: "libvpx", width: width, height: height, frames: frames)))
104	    out.append(("vp9_webm:hlg", settings(
105	        preset: "vp9_webm", writer: "libvpx", color: "hlg", width: width, height: height,
106	        frames: frames)))
107	    out.append(("vp9_alpha_webm", settings(
108	        preset: "vp9_alpha_webm", writer: "libvpx", width: width, height: height,
109	        frames: frames)))
110	    return out
111	}
112	
113	// MARK: - R: the rule
114	
115	let gib: UInt64 = 1 << 30
116	var r1: [[String: Any]] = []
117	for physical in [16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128] {
118	    let ledger = ExportEncoderLedger(physicalMemory: UInt64(physical) * gib)
119	    for (width, height) in [(1920, 1080), (3840, 2160)] {
120	        for (name, s) in keyed(width: width, height: height) {
121	            let fresh = ExportEncoderLedger(physicalMemory: UInt64(physical) * gib)
122	            var admitted = 0
123	            while fresh.admits(s), admitted < 1000 {
124	                _ = fresh.begin(s)
125	                admitted += 1
126	            }
127	            r1.append([
128	                "physicalGiB": physical, "budget": ledger.budget, "key": name,
129	                "width": width, "height": height,
130	                "cost": ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: s, budget: ledger.budget),
131	                "admitted": admitted,
132	            ])
133	        }
134	    }
135	}
136	answer["r1"] = r1
137	
138	do {
139	    let ledger = ExportEncoderLedger(physicalMemory: 64 * gib)
140	    // A writer row with no entry: every real row is measured (codec-export C5's fix pass
141	    // measured vp9_alpha_webm), so the rule is read on a synthetic one.
142	    let alpha = settings(preset: "unmeasured_webm", writer: "libvpx", width: 1920, height: 1080)
143	    let av1 = settings(preset: "av1", writer: "svt_av1", speed: .faster, width: 640, height: 360)
144	    let firstAlpha = ledger.admits(alpha)
145	    let alphaToken = ledger.begin(alpha)
146	    let secondAlpha = ledger.admits(alpha)
147	    let av1Beside = ledger.admits(av1)
148	    let alphaCost = ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: alpha, budget: ledger.budget)
149	    ledger.end(alphaToken)
150	    let av1Token = ledger.begin(av1)
151	    let alphaBesideAV1 = ledger.admits(alpha)
152	    ledger.end(av1Token)
153	    answer["r2"] = [
154	        "budget": ledger.budget, "alphaCost": alphaCost, "firstAdmitted": firstAlpha,
155	        "secondAdmitted": secondAlpha, "av1BesideAlpha": av1Beside,
156	        "alphaBesideAV1": alphaBesideAV1, "idle": ledger.runningCosts.isEmpty,
157	    ]
158	
159	    let h264 = settings(preset: "h264", writer: nil, width: 3840, height: 2160)
160	    let full = ExportEncoderLedger(physicalMemory: 16 * gib)
161	    let held = full.begin(alpha)
162	    let before = full.runningCosts
163	    let h264Token = full.begin(h264)
164	    answer["r3"] = [
165	        "token": h264Token.map { NSNumber(value: $0) } ?? NSNull(),
166	        "admittedBesideFull": full.admits(h264),
167	        "costsUnchanged": full.runningCosts == before,
168	        "cost": ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: h264, budget: full.budget),
169	        "key": ExportEncoderKey(settings: h264) == nil,
170	    ]
171	    full.end(held)
172	}
173	
174	// MARK: - E: the estimate
175	
176	var e1: [[String: Any]] = []
177	for (width, height) in [(1280, 720), (1920, 1080), (2560, 1440), (3840, 2160), (7680, 4320)] {
178	    for frames in [150, 300, 1800] {
179	        for (name, s) in keyed(width: width, height: height, frames: frames) {
180	            e1.append([
181	                "key": name, "width": width, "height": height, "frames": frames,
182	                "seconds": ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds(for: s) ?? NSNull(),
183	                "line": ExportEncoderCosts.sheetLine(for: s) ?? NSNull(),
184	            ])
185	        }
186	    }
187	}
188	answer["e1"] = e1
189	answer["e2"] = [0.4, 2.4, 7.4, 57.4, 59.9, 60, 89, 90, 3569, 3570, 3600, 5399, 5400].map {
190	    ["seconds": $0, "text": ExportEncoderCosts.estimateText(seconds: $0)]
191	}
192	let h264Settings = settings(preset: "h264", writer: nil, width: 1920, height: 1080)
193	// A measured key at a rate that cannot be stepped: no frame count, so no estimate.
194	let unsteppedSettings = settings(
195	    preset: "av1", writer: "svt_av1", speed: .balanced, width: 1920, height: 1080,
196	    fps: [0, 1])
197	answer["e3"] = [
198	    "line": ExportEncoderCosts.sheetLine(for: h264Settings).map { $0 as Any } ?? NSNull(),
199	    "seconds": ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds(for: h264Settings).map { $0 as Any }
200	        ?? NSNull(),
201	    "unsteppedFrames": unsteppedSettings.sequenceFrameCount.map { $0 as Any } ?? NSNull(),
202	    "unsteppedLine": ExportEncoderCosts.sheetLine(for: unsteppedSettings).map { $0 as Any }
203	        ?? NSNull(),
204	    "unsteppedSeconds": ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds(for: unsteppedSettings)
205	        .map { $0 as Any } ?? NSNull(),
206	] as [String: Any]

208	// MARK: - The live projects
209	
210	func apply(_ project: ReelProject, _ op: ReelOp) throws -> ReelProject {
211	    switch try project.applying([op]) {
212	    case .applied(let next): return next
213	    case .identity: return project
214	    case .refused(let refusal): throw ProbeError("\(op.name) was refused: \(refusal.reason)")
215	    }
216	}
217	
218	/// The project with AV.mov in its media, on a canvas of `width` × `height` at 30 fps.
219	func withMedia(width: Int, height: Int) throws -> (ReelProject, UInt32) {
220	    var project = try apply(
221	        ProjectDocument().project, .setCanvas(width: width, height: height, fps: Fps.thirty))
222	    let asset = AVURLAsset(url: media)
223	    let video = asset.tracks(withMediaType: .video).first
224	    let size = video?.naturalSize ?? .zero
225	    let id = project.snapshot.nextId
226	    project = try apply(project, .addMedia(descriptor: MediaDescriptor(
227	        path: media.path, kind: .video, duration: CompositionBuilder.ticks(asset.duration),
228	        width: Int(size.width), height: Int(size.height), fps: Fps.thirty,
229	        hasVideo: video != nil, hasAudio: !asset.tracks(withMediaType: .audio).isEmpty)))
230	    return (project, id)
231	}
232	
233	func a1() throws -> ReelProject {
234	    var (project, id) = try withMedia(width: 640, height: 360)
235	    guard let track = project.snapshot.tracks.first?.id else { throw ProbeError("no track") }
236	    project = try apply(project, .addClip(track: track, media: id, at: 0))
237	    project = try apply(project, .addTrack(index: project.snapshot.tracks.count, name: "Titles"))
238	    guard let titles = project.snapshot.tracks.last?.id else { throw ProbeError("no titles") }
239	    return try apply(project, .addTextClip(
240	        track: titles, at: 0, duration: 2 * ReelTime.perSecond, text: TextPatch(content: "AV1")))
241	}
242	
243	func w9() throws -> ReelProject {
244	    var (project, id) = try withMedia(width: 1920, height: 1080)
245	    guard let track = project.snapshot.tracks.first?.id else { throw ProbeError("no track") }
246	    for k in 0..<24 {
247	        project = try apply(project, .addClip(
248	            track: track, media: id, at: Ticks(k) * 5 * ReelTime.perSecond))
249	    }
250	    let clips = project.snapshot.clips.map(\.id)
251	    return try apply(project, .setVideo(clips: clips, patch: VideoPatch(scale: 3.0)))
252	}
253	
254	func urls(_ project: ReelProject) -> [UInt32: URL] {
255	    var out: [UInt32: URL] = [:]
256	    for item in project.snapshot.media { out[item.id] = URL(fileURLWithPath: item.path) }
257	    return out
258	}
259	
260	func export(
261	    _ project: ReelProject, _ preset: String, speed: EncoderSpeed? = nil
262	) throws -> ExportSettings {
263	    var overrides: [String: Any] = [:]
264	    if let speed { overrides["encoder_speed"] = speed.rawValue }
265	    return try ReelExport.settings(
266	        project, preset: preset, overrides: overrides.isEmpty ? nil : overrides)
267	}
268	
269	func describe(_ s: ExportSettings) -> [String: Any] {
270	    ["preset": s.preset, "writer": s.writer ?? NSNull(), "speed": s.encoderSpeed?.rawValue
271	        ?? NSNull(), "color": s.color ?? NSNull(), "width": s.width, "height": s.height,
272	     "frames": s.sequenceFrameCount ?? 0]
273	}
274	
275	/// A private stored property, by reflection.
276	func reflected<T>(_ object: Any, _ name: String, as: T.Type) -> T? {
277	    Mirror(reflecting: object).children.first { $0.label == name }?.value as? T
278	}
279	
280	func spin(until done: () -> Bool, timeout: Double) -> Bool {
281	    let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(timeout)
282	    while !done(), Date() < deadline {
283	        RunLoop.main.run(mode: .default, before: Date().addingTimeInterval(0.02))
284	    }
285	    return done()
286	}
287	
288	func out(_ name: String) -> URL {
289	    let url = outFolder.appendingPathComponent(name)
290	    try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: url)
291	    return url
292	}
293	
294	func headlessSheet(
295	    _ project: ReelProject, _ settings: ExportSettings, to url: URL
296	) -> ExportProgressSheetController {
297	    let sheet = ExportProgressSheetController(
298	        project: project, urls: urls(project), settings: settings, to: url)
299	    _ = sheet.view
300	    sheet.viewDidAppear()
301	    return sheet
302	}
303	
304	func sheetFinished(_ sheet: ExportProgressSheetController) -> Bool {
305	    reflected(sheet, "didFinish", as: Bool.self) == true
306	}
307	
308	/// What the shared queue and ledger did during a live row: every job's state at each
309	/// change, stamped by a sequence number, and the sequence at which the sheet was first
310	/// seen finished (checked at every change and every spin, before the jobs are read).
311	final class Watch {
312	    let queue = ExportQueueController.shared
313	    var seq = 0
314	    var sheet: ExportProgressSheetController?
315	    var sheetFinishedAt: Int?
316	    var firstSeen: [String: Int] = [:]   // "<id>:<state>" → seq
317	    var ledgerCosts: [[UInt64]] = []
318	    var observers: [NSObjectProtocol] = []
319	
320	    init() {
321	        observers.append(NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
322	            forName: ExportQueueController.didChangeNotification, object: queue, queue: nil
323	        ) { [unowned self] _ in self.tick() })
324	        observers.append(NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
325	            forName: ExportEncoderLedger.didChangeNotification,
326	            object: ExportEncoderLedger.shared, queue: nil
327	        ) { [unowned self] _ in
328	            self.ledgerCosts.append(ExportEncoderLedger.shared.runningCosts)
329	            self.tick()
330	        })
331	    }
332	
333	    func tick() {
334	        seq += 1
335	        if sheetFinishedAt == nil, let sheet, sheetFinished(sheet) { sheetFinishedAt = seq }
336	        for job in queue.jobs {
337	            let key = "\(job.id):\(job.state.rawValue)"
338	            if firstSeen[key] == nil { firstSeen[key] = seq }
339	        }
340	    }
341	
342	    func at(_ id: UInt64, _ state: ExportQueueController.State) -> Any {
343	        firstSeen["\(id):\(state.rawValue)"].map { $0 as Any } ?? NSNull()
344	    }
345	
346	    func job(_ id: UInt64) -> [String: Any] {
347	        let job = queue.job(id)
348	        return [
349	            "state": job?.state.rawValue ?? "missing", "message": job?.message ?? NSNull(),
350	            "waiting": at(id, .waiting), "running": at(id, .running),
351	            "completed": at(id, .completed), "failed": at(id, .failed),
352	        ]
353	    }
354	
355	    func stop() { observers.forEach(NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver) }
356	}
357	
358	// MARK: - Q: the live queue
359	
360	let ledger = ExportEncoderLedger.shared
361	let realPhysical = ledger.physicalMemory
362	var q: [String: Any] = [:]
363	do {
364	    let small = try a1()
365	    let long = try w9()
366	    let sheetSettings = try export(long, "av1", speed: .smaller)
367	    let aSettings = try export(small, "av1")
368	    let hSettings = try export(small, "h264")
369	    q["sheetSettings"] = describe(sheetSettings)
370	    q["aSettings"] = describe(aSettings)
371	
372	    // Q1, Q2, Q4: the budget equal to the sheet job's own cost.
373	    let sheetCost = ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: sheetSettings, budget: 0)
374	    ledger.physicalMemory = 4 * sheetCost
375	    q["q1Physical"] = ledger.physicalMemory
376	    let watch = Watch()
377	    let sheet = headlessSheet(long, sheetSettings, to: out("q1-sheet.mp4"))
378	    watch.sheet = sheet
379	    q["q1Booked"] = ledger.runningCosts
380	    let queue = ExportQueueController.shared
381	    let aURL = out("q1-a.mp4"), bURL = out("q1-b.mp4"), cURL = out("q1-c.mp4")
382	    let a = queue.enqueue(project: small, urls: urls(small), settings: aSettings, to: aURL)
383	    let b = queue.enqueue(project: small, urls: urls(small), settings: hSettings, to: bURL)
384	    let c = queue.enqueue(project: small, urls: urls(small), settings: hSettings, to: cURL)
385	    // Q2 and Q4, read at once: B is running and A held behind the sheet.
386	    q["q4BRunning"] = queue.job(b)?.state == .running
387	    q["q4A"] = queue.job(a).map { ExportQueueRowView.status($0) } ?? NSNull()
388	    q["q4C"] = queue.job(c).map { ExportQueueRowView.status($0) } ?? NSNull()
389	    q["q4ATip"] = queue.job(a).map { ExportQueueRowView.toolTip(for: $0) } ?? NSNull()
390	    q["q4CTip"] = queue.job(c).map { ExportQueueRowView.toolTip(for: $0) } ?? NSNull()
391	    AgentExports.shared.track(
392	        a, settings: aSettings, burnInTimecode: false,
393	        started: ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime)
394	    q["q2"] = AgentExports.shared.status(a) ?? NSNull()
395	    q["q1HeldMessage"] = queue.job(a)?.message ?? NSNull()
396	    let sheetDone = spin(until: { sheetFinished(sheet) }, timeout: 600)
397	    watch.tick()
398	    let drained = spin(until: { queue.isIdle }, timeout: 120)
399	    watch.tick()
400	    q["q1"] = [
401	        "sheetDone": sheetDone, "drained": drained, "sheetFinishedAt": watch.sheetFinishedAt
402	            .map { $0 as Any } ?? NSNull(),
403	        "a": watch.job(a), "b": watch.job(b), "c": watch.job(c),
404	        "files": [aURL, bURL, cURL].map { FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: $0.path) },
405	        "sheetStatus": reflected(sheet, "statusLabel", as: NSTextField.self)?.stringValue
406	            ?? "",
407	    ]
408	    q["q5Drained"] = ledger.runningCosts
409	    watch.stop()
410	
411	    // Q3: a Mac so large nothing waits.
412	    ledger.physicalMemory = 1 << 40
413	    let watch3 = Watch()
414	    let fast = try export(long, "av1", speed: .faster)
415	    let sheet3 = headlessSheet(long, fast, to: out("q3-sheet.mp4"))
416	    watch3.sheet = sheet3
417	    let a3URL = out("q3-a.mp4")
418	    let a3 = queue.enqueue(project: small, urls: urls(small), settings: aSettings, to: a3URL)
419	    let sheet3Done = spin(until: { sheetFinished(sheet3) }, timeout: 600)
420	    watch3.tick()
421	    let drained3 = spin(until: { queue.isIdle }, timeout: 120)
422	    q["q3"] = [
423	        "sheetDone": sheet3Done, "drained": drained3,
424	        "sheetFinishedAt": watch3.sheetFinishedAt.map { $0 as Any } ?? NSNull(),
425	        "a": watch3.job(a3), "file": FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: a3URL.path),
426	    ]
427	    watch3.stop()
428	    q["q5AfterQ3"] = ledger.runningCosts
429	
430	    // Q5: two encoder jobs back to back — the second launches inside the first's `end`.
431	    let x = queue.enqueue(project: small, urls: urls(small), settings: aSettings,
432	                          to: out("q5-x.mp4"))
433	    let y = queue.enqueue(project: small, urls: urls(small), settings: aSettings,
434	                          to: out("q5-y.mp4"))
435	    let drained5 = spin(until: { queue.isIdle }, timeout: 300)
436	    q["q5BackToBack"] = [
437	        "drained": drained5, "x": queue.job(x)?.state.rawValue ?? "missing",
438	        "y": queue.job(y)?.state.rawValue ?? "missing", "costs": ledger.runningCosts,
439	    ]
440	
441	    // Q5: synchronous refusals, in the queue and in a sheet.
442	    guard let empty = ReelProject.new(width: 640, height: 360, fps: Fps.thirty) else {
443	        throw ProbeError("no empty project")
444	    }
445	    // A1's own `av1` settings (the core resolves none for an empty range) over the empty
446	    // handle: `Exporter.export` refuses it synchronously, `emptyTimeline`.
447	    let emptySettings = aSettings
448	    let z = queue.enqueue(project: empty, urls: [:], settings: emptySettings,
449	                          to: out("q5-z.mp4"))
450	    q["q5QueueRefusal"] = [
451	        "state": queue.job(z)?.state.rawValue ?? "missing",
452	        "message": queue.job(z)?.message ?? NSNull(), "costs": ledger.runningCosts,
453	    ]
454	    let refused = headlessSheet(empty, emptySettings, to: out("q5-sheet.mp4"))
455	    q["q5SheetRefusal"] = [
456	        "finished": sheetFinished(refused), "costs": ledger.runningCosts,
457	        "status": reflected(refused, "statusLabel", as: NSTextField.self)?.stringValue ?? "",
458	    ]
459	} catch {
460	    q["error"] = "\(error)"
461	}
462	ledger.physicalMemory = realPhysical
463	answer["q"] = q
464	finish()

1000 / MaxFALL 0 (the walk and the core tests read it), but ffprobe shows only the mastering
  display. A player that reads the light level the same way will see none (HDR-8 asks a person
  to read the metadata).
- **Opus.** AudioToolbox's pre-skip is 312 frames; at 192 kb/s A1's 5 s of sound is 74,132
  bytes (about 119 kb/s; CX-7's undershoot), at 64 kb/s 28,560 (2.60 ×). The tail rule gave the
  exact 240,000 and 96,000 samples on every run.
- **One hang, not reproduced.** In the first mutant pass, while a `cargo test` ran on the same
  machine, the `codec-delay-zero` copy's W8 `sdr` export stopped at progress 0.718 with the
  file at its 430-byte header: `sample` showed the video pump blocked in
  `copyNextSampleBuffer` and the audio pump gone, with no packet written (SVT-AV1 had not yet
  emitted one). That is G-17's starvation: a reader output nobody reads stalls the other. The
  writer now drains the audio output until the video pump has left whenever the audio pump
  stops early (`ExportWebMWriter.drain`). That only narrowed G-17's window; fix pass 1
  replaced it with one reader per output, which closes it for WebM (below). What
  stopped the audio pump was not found: 42 exports of the same project at all three pictures
  (24 on an idle machine, 18 under a CPU load), three whole proof runs logging every stop, and
  every later run (Debug, every mutant copy, Release) showed no failure and no hang. Filed
  below as owed.
- The proof's own first mutant runner ran the whole `export_offset_proof.py` for every mutant
  (an empty `--only` is every row); the offset path was dropped with `codec-delay-zero`'s E38
  and E39.

  core also writes the WebM an export makes ("… the index of a WebM/Matroska file being
  imported and the WebM file an `av1_webm` export writes").

  `light_from_clli`.

  `ExportWebMLayout.swift`, `ExportOpusEncoder.swift` and `ExportPacketSink.swift`, and

  gains `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`); the `DispatchQueue` seams (line 3156) gain the WebM writer's
  two queues (`com.kgalligan.framejob.export.webm.video` and `.audio`), beside
  `ExportWriter`'s; `ExportAudioEnd.swift`'s entry gains `align` (the WebM writer's
  placement by stamp, fix pass 1); the export entry also gains `ExportWebMDevFault.swift`

  output, each cancelled by its own pump (CX-15 (2)).

  `-RCDevSyncHold` and `-RCDevRampRenderHold`): `-RCDevWebMFault audio@N|video@N|audio-hold@N`,
  which puts a fault in an `av1_webm` export's audio pump or video sink so a proof can time
  the stop (fix pass 1).

**Fix pass 1 (the review and the orchestrator's ruling, 2026-10-28).**
- **G-17 on the WebM path: closed, by one `AVAssetReader` per output (ruling 2).** Ruling 1
  first asked for `reader.cancelReading()` from the stopping thread; that was stopped:
  AVFoundation's `AVAssetReader.h` says of `cancelReading` "This method should not be called
  concurrently with any calls to -[AVAssetReaderOutput copyNextSampleBuffer]", and G-17
  measured exactly that call crashing 12 of 30 mid-export cancels (road map 10 §10.6 G3c).
  Ruling 2 took the fix this pass proposed instead. `ExportWebMWriter` now gives the video
  composition output and the audio mix output each a reader of its own over the same
  composition and range (a silent movie has the video reader alone); each pump, after its
  own last read on a stop, cancels its own reader on its own queue (the video reader's
  cancel is a block on `videoQueue` after `ExportEncodePump`'s read loop, inside the pumps'
  group; the audio pump's follows `pumpAudio`). No thread cancels another's reader, and
  `allPumpsLeft` cancels none. `drain` and `videoLeft` are gone: they existed only for the
  shared reader's coupling. `ExportEncodePump` and the MP4 path are untouched.

# ---- the probe ------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_probe(sources, folder):
    """The probe built over `sources` in `folder`: (binary, "") or (None, why)."""
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    entry = folder / "main.swift"
    text = PROBE_SWIFT.read_text()
    if not entry.exists() or entry.read_text() != text:
        entry.write_text(text)
    resources = ROOT / "app" / "Resources"
    shutil.copy2(resources / "Blank.mp4", folder / "Blank.mp4")
    shutil.copytree(resources / "Fonts", folder / "Fonts", dirs_exist_ok=True)
    airs = []
    for shader in ("Compositor", "ExportI010"):
        air = folder / f"{shader}.air"
        step = bounded.run(["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metal", "-c",
                            str(resources / "Shaders" / f"{shader}.metal"), "-o", str(air)], 300)
        if step["rc"] != 0:
            return None, f"{shader}.metal did not build: {step['stderr'][-300:]}"
        airs.append(str(air))
    step = bounded.run(["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metallib", *airs, "-o",
                        str(folder / "default.metallib")], 300)
    if step["rc"] != 0:
        return None, f"the metallib did not build: {step['stderr'][-300:]}"
    binary = folder / "encoder-limit-probe"
    try:
        built = swift_build.build(sources=swift_build.app_sources(sources) + [entry],
                                  output=binary, defines=["FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS"], timeout=900)
    except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error:
        lines = [line for line in error.diagnostics if ": error:" in line]
        return None, "the probe did not build: " + " | ".join(
            lines[:3] or list(error.diagnostics[:3]) or [str(error)])
    print(f"  probe: up to date — {binary}" if built.reused
          else f"  probe: built in {built.seconds:.0f} s — {binary}", flush=True)
    return binary, ""


def run_probe(sources=SOURCES, folder=None):
    """B0 and every probe row, from one probe run over `sources`."""
    folder = folder or WORK / "probe"
    binary, why = build_probe(Path(sources), folder)
    if binary is None:
        for ident in PROBE_ROWS:
            check(ident, False, why)
        return None
    answer_path, out = folder / "answer.json", folder / "out"
    answer_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    ran = bounded.run([str(binary), str(av1.AV), str(out), str(answer_path)], 1500,
                      cwd=str(folder))
    if ran["expired"] or ran["rc"] != 0 or not answer_path.exists():
        why = "the probe did not run: " + (ran["stdout"] + ran["stderr"]).strip()[-400:]
        for ident in PROBE_ROWS:
            check(ident, False, why)
        return None
    answer = json.loads(answer_path.read_text())
    check("B0", True, f"built and answered ({folder})")
    score_probe(answer)
    return answer


def score_probe(answer):
    tables = Tables(answer)
    finally:
        instance.stop()


# ---- mutants and main -----------------------------------------------------------------

def run_mutant(name):
    if name not in MUTANTS:
        print(f"unknown mutant {name}; the mutants are {sorted(MUTANTS)}")
        return 2
    named, edits = MUTANTS[name]
    copy = WORK / "mutant" / name
    sources = copy / "Sources"
    shutil.rmtree(copy, ignore_errors=True)
    shutil.copytree(SOURCES, sources)
    for file, anchor, replacement in edits:
        target = sources / file
        text = target.read_text()
        if text.count(anchor) != 1:
            print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — the anchor occurs "
                  f"{text.count(anchor)} times in {file}")
            return 2
        target.write_text(text.replace(anchor, replacement))
    answer = run_probe(sources, WORK / "mutant-probe" / name)
    if answer is None:
        print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — the probe failed whole")
        return 2
    failing = sorted(k for k, v in results.items() if not v)
    print(f"mutant {name}: named {named}, failing {failing}")
    if all(results.get(row) is False for row in named):
        print(f"MUTANT CAUGHT: {name}")
        return 1
    print(f"MUTANT SURVIVED: {name}")
    return 0

input.content:
# Objections

## 1
- **Risk category:** correctness
- **Claim:** As placed, the counters cannot detect a lost request, so branch L has no observable signature, and a real lost request would be classified as A ("AVF never asked"). The table's L row, "`begun > done` and no Compositor frame", cannot occur: `done()` is a `defer` in the same block that counted `begun()`. So `begun > done` means a block is still running `serve` on `renderQueue`, and its frames would be in the sample.
- **Evidence:** In spec line 10, `begun()` and `defer { done() }` both sit in the `renderQueue` block. In `app/Sources/Compositor.swift:188-198` that block exits, and `done` increments, whether or not `request.finish*` was called. Spec line 91 is the L row; spec line 93 reads `asked == done` as "AVF never asked". A block that returned without answering leaves `asked == begun == done` and lands in row A. A block stuck inside `serve` (in `RecipeSource.recipe`, `renderer.render` or `newPixelBuffer`) gives `begun > done` with Compositor frames present, which matches no row at all.
- **Suggested change:** Add an `answered` counter at each `finish(withComposedVideoFrame:)`, `finish(with:)` and `finishCancelledRequest` call, define L as `done > answered` (or `asked > answered` with `begun == done`), and add a row for `begun > done` (a request blocked in `serve`) that names the frame it is blocked in.

## 2
- **Risk category:** correctness
- **Claim:** The variant rule is undefined, and can fail open, when the baseline has 1–2 stalls, or when the stalls come only from app mode. Variants run only in probe mode, so if the probe never stalled, every variant "removes" a stall it never had.
- **Evidence:** Spec lines 84–85 stop only at zero stalls in total. With 1–2 stalls after the `--load 36` top-up, step 4's "as many runs as the baseline needed for 3 stalls" (line 94) has no value. `--variant` is defined only for `probe` mode (line 68). Scenario: probe has 0 of 40 runs stalled and app has 3 of 20. Every variant then runs 30 probe runs with 0 stalls and counts as "removes", and step 6 picks a branch on noise. The rate can be this low: the record (`designs/codec-export.md:1376-1386`, `:1962-1965`) shows 1 hang in 3 probe runs, then 13/13 at once, and 0 in 42 earlier.
- **Suggested change:** Score each variant against the baseline of the mode it runs in: allow probe-mode variants only when the probe baseline itself reached 3 stalls, and add a STOP for the case where the stalling mode reached fewer than 3 (or where only app mode stalled).

## 3
- **Risk category:** under-scope
- **Claim:** `defer-launch`, and the R fix it stands for, defer only the ledger-notification path. `ExportQueueController.finished` still calls `start()` straight after `end`, so a queue-to-queue launch still runs inside the previous `Exporter`'s completion callback. That is the same re-entrancy, and it is the path the soak's step 4 and the probe's Q5 exercise.
- **Evidence:** `app/Sources/ExportQueueController.swift:261` is `ledgerChanged → start()`. In `:489-493`, `ledger.end(token)` is followed by a direct `start()`, all inside `Exporter.finish`'s `completion?(result)` (`app/Sources/Exporter.swift` `finish`). Under the variant, Q5's y (spec line 76, "Q5's re-entrant launch") is still launched from x's completion stack through line 493. Today it is launched through the notification. If R is the cause, the variant clears Q1's stalls and not Q5's, the per-run summary cannot tell them apart, and R is either rejected or fixed only halfway.
- **Suggested change:** Make `defer-launch`, and the R fix's rule, defer every launch made from a finishing export, both `ledgerChanged` and the `start()` at `ExportQueueController.swift:493`, to the next main turn, and have Q6 cover the queue-to-queue case too.

## 4
- **Risk category:** missing-edge-case
- **Claim:** App mode never checks that a run actually reached the scenario under test, where A is held behind a booked sheet and then launched inside the sheet's `end`. A run that misses it still counts as `done`, which inflates the denominator that STOP-1 and the after-fix "0 stalls" rest on.
- **Evidence:** The sheet books only in `viewDidAppear` (`app/Sources/ExportProgressSheetController.swift:111-116`). `beginExport` only calls `presentAsSheet` (`app/Sources/EditorViewController+Export.swift:55-60`), so the booking is not guaranteed to exist when `export_sheet begin` returns. Spec lines 53 and 73–74 answer `booked` but never require it to be non-empty before step 2's `export` of A. If A runs before the sheet books, it is admitted at once, so it is never held and never launched in `end`. The run then finishes as `done`.
- **Suggested change:** Make the soak count an app run as `error`, not `done`, unless `begin` answered a `booked` that holds the sheet's cost and A was seen `queued` with the ledger's waiting message before the sheet finished.

## 5
- **Risk category:** missing-edge-case
- **Claim:** `summary.json` does not record which job or row stalled. With the default `--stall-s 120`, equal to the probe's own Q1 drain timeout, a Q1 stall is usually caught later, during Q3 or Q5, so the trace's last line names the wrong row. The branch table and objection 3's scoring both depend on which launch path hung.
- **Evidence:** In `tools/proof/encoder_limit_probe.swift:396-398`, the Q1 drain spin gives up after 120 s and the probe moves on. Q3's `enqueue` (`:418`) and Q5's (`:431-434`) add new job states, which reset the stall clock (spec line 62). Only Q5's 300 s spin (`:435`) outlasts 120 s. So the sample is taken minutes later, the "last" trace counts include Q3's sheet, and spec line 67 lists no row or job at all.
- **Suggested change:** Have the runner record, for each stall, the id and row of the job whose progress stopped first, taken from the trace's first unchanged line, and let a probe knob lengthen the probe's spin timeouts past `--stall-s`.

verdict: revise
